1.81.s:
śrīsanatkumāra uvāca /
atha kṛṣṇasya mantrāṇāṃ vakṣye bhedān munīśvara /
yānsamārādhya manujāḥ sādhayantīṣṭamātmanaḥ //
1.81.d:
श्रीसनत्कुमार उवाच ।
अथ कृष्णस्य मन्त्राणां वक्ष्ये भेदान् मुनीश्वर ।
यान्समाराध्य मनुजाः साधयन्तीष्टमात्मनः ॥
1.81.m: Śrī Sanatkumāra said: / Now I shall speak of the varieties of Kṛṣṇa's mantras, O best of sages, / By worshipping which human beings accomplish their desired aims.

1.81.s:
śaktiśrīmārapūrvaśca śrīśaktismarapūrvakaḥ /
māraśaktiramāpūrvo daśārṇā manavastrayaḥ //
1.81.d:
शक्तिश्रीमारपूर्वश्च श्रीशक्तिस्मरपूर्वकः ।
मारशक्तिरमापूर्वो दशार्णा मनवस्त्रयः ॥
1.81.m: Preceded by Śakti, Śrī, and Māra; preceded by Śrī, Śakti, and Smara; / and preceded by Māra, Śakti, and Ramā—these are three ten-syllable mantras.

1.81.s:
muniḥ syānnā radacchando gāyatrī devatā punaḥ /
kṛṣṇo govindanāmātra sarvakāmaprado nṛṇām //
1.81.d:
मुनिः स्यान्ना रदच्छन्दो गायत्री देवता पुनः ।
कृष्णो गोविन्दनामात्र सर्वकामप्रदो नृणाम् ॥
1.81.m: The sage is Nārada, the meter is gāyatrī, and the deity / is Kṛṣṇa under the name Govinda, granting all desires to men here.

1.81.s:
cakraiḥ pūrvavadaṅgāni trayāṇāmapi kalpayet /
tataḥ kirīṭamanunāvyāpakaṃ hi samācaret //
1.81.d:
चक्रैः पूर्ववदङ्गानि त्रयाणामपि कल्पयेत् ।
ततः किरीटमनुनाव्यापकं हि समाचरेत् ॥
1.81.m: One should fashion the limbs for all three with the discs, as previously told; / then, indeed, one should perform the comprehensive placement with the Kirīṭa-mantra.

1.81.s:
sudarśanasya manunā kuryāddigbandhanaṃ tathā /
viṃśatyarṇoktavatkuryādādye dhyānārcanādikam //
1.81.d:
सुदर्शनस्य मनुना कुर्याद्दिग्बन्धनं तथा ।
विंशत्यर्णोक्तवत्कुर्यादाद्ये ध्यानार्चनादिकम् ॥
1.81.m: One should likewise perform the binding of the directions with the mantra of Sudarśana. / For the first, one should perform the meditation, worship, and the rest as taught for the twenty-syllable [mantra].

1.81.s:
dvitīye tu daśārṇoktaṃ dhyānapūjādikaṃ caret /
tṛtīye tu hariṃ dhyāyetsamāhitamanāḥ sudhīḥ //
1.81.d:
द्वितीये तु दशार्णोक्तं ध्यानपूजादिकं चरेत् ।
तृतीये तु हरिं ध्यायेत्समाहितमनाः सुधीः ॥
1.81.m: For the second, one should perform the meditation, worship, and so forth taught for the ten-syllable [mantra]. / For the third, the wise person, with collected mind, should meditate on Hari:

1.81.s:
śakhacakradhanurbāṇapāśāṅkuśadharāruṇam /
dorbhyāṃ dhṛtaṃ dhamantaṃ ca veṇuṃ kṛṣṇadivākaram //
1.81.d:
शखचक्रधनुर्बाणपाशाङ्कुशधरारुणम् ।
दोर्भ्यां धृतं धमन्तं च वेणुं कृष्णदिवाकरम् ॥
1.81.m: Holding the conch, discus, bow, arrows, noose, and goad, reddish, / holding with two hands and blowing the flute, Kṛṣṇa, radiant like the sun.

1.81.s:
evaṃ dhyātvā japenmantrānpañcalakṣaṃ pṛthak sudhīḥ /
juhuyāttaddaśāṃśena pāyasena sasarpiṣā //
1.81.d:
एवं ध्यात्वा जपेन्मन्त्रान्पञ्चलक्षं पृथक् सुधीः ।
जुहुयात्तद्दशांशेन पायसेन ससर्पिषा ॥
1.81.m: Meditating thus, the wise person should recite each of the mantras separately five hundred thousand times, / and should make fire oblation with a tenth of that with milk-rice mixed with ghee.

1.81.s:
evaṃ siddhe manau mantrī kuryātkāmyāni pūrvavat /
śrīśaktikāmaḥ kṛṣṇāya govindāyāgnisundarī //
1.81.d:
एवं सिद्धे मनौ मन्त्री कुर्यात्काम्यानि पूर्ववत् ।
श्रीशक्तिकामः कृष्णाय गोविन्दायाग्निसुन्दरी ॥
1.81.m: When the mantra is thus mastered, the practitioner should perform optional rites as before. / [The mantra begins with] Śrī, Śakti, Kāma, [followed by] 'to Kṛṣṇa', 'to Govinda', [and] the wife of Agni [Svāhā].

1.81.s:
ratryarṇo brahmagāyatrīkṛṣṇā ṛṣyādayo 'sya tu /
bījairamābdhiyugmārṇaiḥ ṣaḍaṅgāni prakalpayet //
1.81.d:
रत्र्यर्णो ब्रह्मगायत्रीकृष्णा ऋष्यादयो ऽस्य तु ।
बीजैरमाब्धियुग्मार्णैः षडङ्गानि प्रकल्पयेत् ॥
1.81.m: It has sixteen syllables; its sage and other [adjuncts] are Brahmā, gāyatrī, and Kṛṣṇa. / With seed-syllables consisting of pairs of four syllables, one should fashion the six limbs.

1.81.s:
viṃśatyarṇoditajapadhyānahomārcanādikam /
kiṃ bahūktena mantro 'yaṃ sarvābhīṣṭaphalapradaḥ //
1.81.d:
विंशत्यर्णोदितजपध्यानहोमार्चनादिकम् ।
किं बहूक्तेन मन्त्रो ऽयं सर्वाभीष्टफलप्रदः ॥
1.81.m: Recitation, meditation, fire oblation, worship, and the rest are as stated for the twenty-syllable [mantra]. / What need is there to say much? This mantra bestows the fruit of all desires.

1.81.s:
śrīśaktismarapūrvogajanmā śaktiramāntikaḥ /
daśākṣaraḥ sa evādau proktaḥ śaktiramāyutaḥ //
1.81.d:
श्रीशक्तिस्मरपूर्वोगजन्मा शक्तिरमान्तिकः ।
दशाक्षरः स एवादौ प्रोक्तः शक्तिरमायुतः ॥
1.81.m: Preceded by Śrī, Śakti, and Smara, ending with Śakti and Ramā, / the ten-syllable mantra is that very one previously stated, combined with Śakti and Ramā.

1.81.s:
mantrau ṣoḍaśaravyārṇauṃ cakrairaṅgāni kalpayet /
varadābhayahastābhyāṃ śliṣyantaṃ svāṅgake priye //
1.81.d:
मन्त्रौ षोडशरव्यार्णौं चक्रैरङ्गानि कल्पयेत् ।
वरदाभयहस्ताभ्यां श्लिष्यन्तं स्वाङ्गके प्रिये ॥
1.81.m: These two mantras have sixteen and twelve syllables; one should assign their limbs with the discs. / Embracing his beloved upon his own body with hands conferring boons and fearlessness,

1.81.s:
padmotpalakare tābhyāṃ śliṣṭaṃ cakradarojvalam /
dhyātvaivaṃ prajapellakṣadaśakaṃ taddaśāṃśataḥ //
1.81.d:
पद्मोत्पलकरे ताभ्यां श्लिष्टं चक्रदरोज्वलम् ।
ध्यात्वैवं प्रजपेल्लक्षदशकं तद्दशांशतः ॥
1.81.m: embraced by the two [hands] holding a lotus and a water-lily, radiant with discus and conch— / having meditated thus, one should recite it one million times, [and] with one-tenth of that,

1.81.s:
ājyairhutvā tataḥ siddhau bhavetāṃ mantranāyakau /
sarvakāmapradau sarvasaṃpatsaubhagāgyadau nṛṇām //
1.81.d:
आज्यैर्हुत्वा ततः सिद्धौ भवेतां मन्त्रनायकौ ।
सर्वकामप्रदौ सर्वसंपत्सौभगाग्यदौ नृणाम् ॥
1.81.m: having made fire oblations with clarified butter, these two sovereign mantras then become perfected. / They grant all desires, and bestow all prosperity and good fortune on men.

1.81.s:
aṣṭādaśārṇaḥ kāmānto manuḥ sutadhanapradaḥ /
nārado 'sya muniśchando gāyatrī devatā manoḥ //
1.81.d:
अष्टादशार्णः कामान्तो मनुः सुतधनप्रदः ।
नारदो ऽस्य मुनिश्छन्दो गायत्री देवता मनोः ॥
1.81.m: The eighteen-syllable mantra ending with Kāma bestows sons and wealth; / Nārada is its sage, the meter is gāyatrī, and the deity of the mantra is

1.81.s:
kṛṣṇaḥ kāmo bījamuktaṃ śaktirvahnipriyā matā /
ṣaḍvīryāḍhyena bījena ṣaḍaṅgāni samācaret //
1.81.d:
कृष्णः कामो बीजमुक्तं शक्तिर्वह्निप्रिया मता ।
षड्वीर्याढ्येन बीजेन षडङ्गानि समाचरेत् ॥
1.81.m: Kṛṣṇa; Kāma is declared the seed-syllable, and the beloved of Agni [Svāhā] is considered the śakti. / One should perform the six limbs with the seed-syllable endowed with the six powers.

1.81.s:
pāṇau pāyasapakvaṃ ca dakṣe haiyaṅgavīnakam /
vāme dadhaddivyadigaṃbaro gopīsuto 'vatu //
1.81.d:
पाणौ पायसपक्वं च दक्षे हैयङ्गवीनकम् ।
वामे दधद्दिव्यदिगंबरो गोपीसुतो ऽवतु ॥
1.81.m: Holding cooked milk-rice in his left hand, and fresh butter in his right, / sky-clad, heavenly, may the son of the cowherdess protect [us]!

1.81.s:
dhyātvaivaṃ prajapenmantraṃ dvātriṃśallakṣamānataḥ /
daśāṃśaṃ juhuyādagnau sitāḍhyena payoṃ'dhasā //
1.81.d:
ध्यात्वैवं प्रजपेन्मन्त्रं द्वात्रिंशल्लक्षमानतः ।
दशांशं जुहुयादग्नौ सिताढ्येन पयोंऽधसा ॥
1.81.m: Having meditated thus, one should recite the mantra according to the measure of three million two hundred thousand times; / one should offer in the fire a tenth of that with milk-porridge mixed with sugar.

1.81.s:
pūrvoktavaiṣṇave pīṭhe yajedaṣṭādaśārṇavat /
padmasthaṃ kṛṣṇamabhyarcya tarpayettanmukhāṃbuje //
1.81.d:
पूर्वोक्तवैष्णवे पीठे यजेदष्टादशार्णवत् ।
पद्मस्थं कृष्णमभ्यर्च्य तर्पयेत्तन्मुखांबुजे ॥
1.81.m: Upon the previously mentioned Vaiṣṇava ritual seat, one should worship [him] as for the eighteen-syllable [mantra]. / Having worshipped Kṛṣṇa seated on a lotus, one should offer satiation into his lotus mouth

1.81.s:
kṣīreṇa kadalīpakkairdadhnā haiyaṅgavena ca /
putrārthī tarpayedevaṃ vatsarāllabhate sutam //
1.81.d:
क्षीरेण कदलीपक्कैर्दध्ना हैयङ्गवेन च ।
पुत्रार्थी तर्पयेदेवं वत्सराल्लभते सुतम् ॥
1.81.m: with milk, ripe plantains, curds, and fresh butter. / One desiring a son who makes satiations in this way obtains a son within a year.

1.81.s:
yadyadicchati tatsarvaṃ tarpaṇādeva siddhyati /
vākkāmo ṅeyutaṃ kṛṣṇapadaṃ māyā tataḥ pagaram //
1.81.d:
यद्यदिच्छति तत्सर्वं तर्पणादेव सिद्ध्यति ।
वाक्कामो ङेयुतं कृष्णपदं माया ततः पगरम् ॥
1.81.m: Whatever one desires, all that is accomplished simply through satiation. / The Vāc [bīja], the Kāma [bīja], the word 'Kṛṣṇa' in the dative, then Māyā, then [the word]

1.81.s:
govindāya ramā paścāddaśārṇaṃ ca samuddharet /
manusvarayutau sargayuktau bhṛgutadūrddhūgau //
1.81.d:
गोविन्दाय रमा पश्चाद्दशार्णं च समुद्धरेत् ।
मनुस्वरयुतौ सर्गयुक्तौ भृगुतदूर्द्धूगौ ॥
1.81.m: Govinda in the dative, Ramā, and thereafter one should extract the ten syllables: / the Bhṛgu letter along with the seventh vowel and accompanied by the visarga, and the letter above it—

1.81.s:
dvāviṃśatyakṣaro mantro vāgīśatvapradāyakaḥ /
ṛṣiḥ syānnāradaśchando gāyatrī devatā punaḥ //
1.81.d:
द्वाविंशत्यक्षरो मन्त्रो वागीशत्वप्रदायकः ।
ऋषिः स्यान्नारदश्छन्दो गायत्री देवता पुनः ॥
1.81.m: this twenty-two-syllable mantra bestows mastery of speech. / The sage is Nārada, the meter is gāyatrī, and the deity

1.81.s:
vidyāpradaśca gopālaḥ kāmo bījaṃ prakīrtitam /
śaktistu vāgbhavaṃ vidyāprāptaye viniyojanā //
1.81.d:
विद्याप्रदश्च गोपालः कामो बीजं प्रकीर्तितम् ।
शक्तिस्तु वाग्भवं विद्याप्राप्तये विनियोजना ॥
1.81.m: is Gopāla, the giver of learning; Kāma is proclaimed the seed-syllable, / and the Vāgbhava [bīja] is the śakti; its application is for obtaining knowledge.

1.81.s:
vāmorddhvahaste dadhataṃ vidyāpustakamuttamam /
akṣamālāṃ ca dakṣorddhvasphaāṭikīṃ mātṛkāmayīm //
1.81.d:
वामोर्द्ध्वहस्ते दधतं विद्यापुस्तकमुत्तमम् ।
अक्षमालां च दक्षोर्द्ध्वस्फआटिकीं मातृकामयीम् ॥
1.81.m: Holding the excellent book of knowledge in his upper left hand, / and in his upper right a rosary of crystal composed of the letters of the alphabet,

1.81.s:
śabdabrahma mayaṃ veṇumadhaḥ pāṇidvaye punaḥ /
gāyatrīgītavasanaṃ śyāmalaṃ komalacchavim //
1.81.d:
शब्दब्रह्म मयं वेणुमधः पाणिद्वये पुनः ।
गायत्रीगीतवसनं श्यामलं कोमलच्छविम् ॥
1.81.m: and then in his lower two hands the flute made of the Sound-Brahman, / clothed in the songs of the gāyatrī, dark-hued, of delicate beauty,

1.81.s:
barhāvataṃsaṃ sarvajñaṃ sevitaṃ munipuṅgavaiḥ /
dhyātvaivaṃ pramadāveśavilāsaṃ bhuvaneśvaram //
1.81.d:
बर्हावतंसं सर्वज्ञं सेवितं मुनिपुङ्गवैः ।
ध्यात्वैवं प्रमदावेशविलासं भुवनेश्वरम् ॥
1.81.m: with a peacock-feather ornament, omniscient, attended by eminent sages— / having thus meditated on the Lord of the world, indulging in amorous play with passionate women,

1.81.s:
vedalakṣaṃ japenmantraṃ kiṃśukaistaddaśāṃśataḥ /
hutvā tu pūjayenmantrī viṃśatyarṇavidhānataḥ //
1.81.d:
वेदलक्षं जपेन्मन्त्रं किंशुकैस्तद्दशांशतः ।
हुत्वा तु पूजयेन्मन्त्री विंशत्यर्णविधानतः ॥
1.81.m: the practitioner should recite the mantra four hundred thousand times; / and having made fire oblations with kiṃśuka flowers for a tenth of that, he should worship according to the rule of the twenty-syllable [mantra].

1.81.s:
evaṃ yo bhajate mantraṃ bhavedvāgīśvarastu saḥ /
adṛṣṭānyapi śāstrāṇi tasya gaṅgātaraṅgavat //
1.81.d:
एवं यो भजते मन्त्रं भवेद्वागीश्वरस्तु सः ।
अदृष्टान्यपि शास्त्राणि तस्य गङ्गातरङ्गवत् ॥
1.81.m: He who serves this mantra in this way becomes a master of speech; / even unstudied scriptures [flow from] him like the waves of the Gaṅgā.

1.81.s:
tāraḥ kṛṣṇayugaṃ paścānmahākṛṣṇa itīrayet /
sarvajña tvaṃpraśaṃśabdānte sīdame 'gniśca māram //
1.81.d:
तारः कृष्णयुगं पश्चान्महाकृष्ण इतीरयेत् ।
सर्वज्ञ त्वंप्रशंशब्दान्ते सीदमे ऽग्निश्च मारम् ॥
1.81.m: One should utter the pranava, a pair of Kṛṣṇas, and next 'mahākṛṣṇa'; / then the words 'sarvajña tvaṃ praśanna', 'me', and the fire-wife with Kāma;

1.81.s:
ṇānti vidyeśa vidyāmāśu prayaccha tataśca me /
trayastriṃśadakṣaro 'yaṃ mahāvidyāpradomanuḥ //
1.81.d:
णान्ति विद्येश विद्यामाशु प्रयच्छ ततश्च मे ।
त्रयस्त्रिंशदक्षरो ऽयं महाविद्याप्रदोमनुः ॥
1.81.m: ending in 'ṇā', then 'vidyeśa vidyām āśu prayaccha me'. / This is a thirty-three-syllable mantra that bestows great knowledge.

1.81.s:
nārado 'sya muniśchando 'nuṣṭum kṛṣṇo 'sya devatā /
pādaiḥ sarveṇa pañcāṅgaṃ kṛtvā dhyāyettato harim //
1.81.d:
नारदो ऽस्य मुनिश्छन्दो ऽनुष्टुम् कृष्णो ऽस्य देवता ।
पादैः सर्वेण पञ्चाङ्गं कृत्वा ध्यायेत्ततो हरिम् ॥
1.81.m: Nārada is its seer, the metre is anuṣṭubh, and Kṛṣṇa is its deity. / Having performed the five limbs with its quarters and the whole, one should then meditate upon Hari:

1.81.s:
divyodyāne vivasvatpratimamaṇimaye maṇḍape yogapīṭhe madhye yaḥ sarvavedāntamayasurataroḥ saṃniviṣṭo mukundaḥ /
vedaiḥ kalpadrurūpaiḥ śikhariśatasamālaṃbikośaiścaturbhirnyāyaistarkaipurāṇaiḥ smṛtibhirabhivṛtastādṛśaiścāmarādyaiḥ //
1.81.d:
दिव्योद्याने विवस्वत्प्रतिममणिमये मण्डपे योगपीठे मध्ये यः सर्ववेदान्तमयसुरतरोः संनिविष्टो मुकुन्दः ।
वेदैः कल्पद्रुरूपैः शिखरिशतसमालंबिकोशैश्चतुर्भिर्न्यायैस्तर्कैपुराणैः स्मृतिभिरभिवृतस्तादृशैश्चामराद्यैः ॥
1.81.m: 'Mukunda, seated upon a yoga-seat in a jewelled pavilion resembling the sun in a divine garden, / amidst the wish-fulfilling tree composed of all the Upaniṣads, surrounded by the four Vedas in the form of wish-granting trees whose repositories rest upon hundreds of mountain peaks, / by the Nyāya systems, dialectics, Purāṇas, and Smṛtis, which are similarly attended with chowries and the like;

1.81.s:
dadyādbibhratkarāgrairapi daramuralīpuṣpabāṇekṣucāpānakṣaspṛkpūrṇakuṃbhau smaralalitavapurdivyabhūṣāṅgarāgaḥ /
vyākhyāṃ vāme vitanvan sphuṭarucirapado veṇunā viśvamātre śabdabrahmodbhavena śriyamaruṇarucirballavīvallabho naḥ //
1.81.d:
दद्याद्बिभ्रत्कराग्रैरपि दरमुरलीपुष्पबाणेक्षुचापानक्षस्पृक्पूर्णकुंभौ स्मरललितवपुर्दिव्यभूषाङ्गरागः ।
व्याख्यां वामे वितन्वन् स्फुटरुचिरपदो वेणुना विश्वमात्रे शब्दब्रह्मोद्भवेन श्रियमरुणरुचिर्बल्लवीवल्लभो नः ॥
1.81.m: holding in his fingertips the conch, flute, flower-arrows, and sugarcane bow, / touching a rosary and full jar, his body charming like the god of love, adorned with divine ornaments and unguents, / displaying the gesture of exposition with his left hand, his clear and radiant feet [resplendent], the lover of cowherd women, glowing with dawn-like radiance, / who through his flute bestows prosperity born of the sound-Brahman upon the entire universe, may he grant [prosperity] to us.'

1.81.s:
evaṃ dhyātvā japellakṣaṃ daśāṃśaṃ pāyasairhunet /
aṣṭādaśārṇavatkuryādyajanaṃ cāsya mantravit //
1.81.d:
एवं ध्यात्वा जपेल्लक्षं दशांशं पायसैर्हुनेत् ।
अष्टादशार्णवत्कुर्याद्यजनं चास्य मन्त्रवित् ॥
1.81.m: Meditating thus, one should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times, and offer a tenth of that in fire oblations with milk-rice. / The knower of mantras should perform his worship as prescribed for the eighteen-syllable [mantra].

1.81.s:
tāro namo bhagavate nandaputrāya saṃvadet /
ānandavapuṣe dadyādṛśārṇaṃ tadanantaram //
1.81.d:
तारो नमो भगवते नन्दपुत्राय संवदेत् ।
आनन्दवपुषे दद्यादृशार्णं तदनन्तरम् ॥
1.81.m: One should say the pranava, 'namo bhagavate nandaputrāya', / and 'ānandavapuṣe', and immediately thereafter one should add the ten-syllable [mantra].

1.81.s:
aṣṭāviṃśativarṇo 'yaṃ mantraḥ sarveṣṭadāyakaḥ /
nandaputrapadaṃ ṅeṃtaṃ śyāmalāṅgapadaṃ tathā //
1.81.d:
अष्टाविंशतिवर्णो ऽयं मन्त्रः सर्वेष्टदायकः ।
नन्दपुत्रपदं ङेंतं श्यामलाङ्गपदं तथा ॥
1.81.m: This twenty-eight-syllable mantra grants all desired objects. / Or the word 'nandaputra' ending in the dative, then the word 'śyāmalāṅga',

1.81.s:
tathā bālavapuḥkṛṣṇaṃ govindaṃ ca tathā punaḥ /
daśārṇo 'to bhavenmantro dvātriṃśadakṣarānvitaḥ //
1.81.d:
तथा बालवपुःकृष्णं गोविन्दं च तथा पुनः ।
दशार्णो ऽतो भवेन्मन्त्रो द्वात्रिंशदक्षरान्वितः ॥
1.81.m: and then 'bālavapuṣe kṛṣṇāya' and again 'govindāya'; / with the ten-syllable [mantra] added to this, it becomes a mantra endowed with thirty-two syllables.

1.81.s:
anayornāradaṛṣiśchandastūṣṇiganuṣṭubhau /
devatā nandaputrastu viniyogo 'khilāptaye //
1.81.d:
अनयोर्नारदऋषिश्छन्दस्तूष्णिगनुष्टुभौ ।
देवता नन्दपुत्रस्तु विनियोगो ऽखिलाप्तये ॥
1.81.m: Of these two, Nārada is the seer, the metres are uṣṇih and anuṣṭubh, / the deity is the son of Nanda, and the ritual application is for the attainment of all ends.

1.81.s:
cakraiḥ pañcāṅgamarcāsyādaṅgadikpālahetibhiḥ /
dakṣiṇe ratnacaṣakaṃ vāme sauvarṇanetrakam //
1.81.d:
चक्रैः पञ्चाङ्गमर्चास्यादङ्गदिक्पालहेतिभिः ।
दक्षिणे रत्नचषकं वामे सौवर्णनेत्रकम् ॥
1.81.m: The five-limb worship is performed with the disc-syllables, accompanied by the limbs, guardians of the directions, and their weapons. / One should meditate on the Lord holding a jewel goblet in his right hand

1.81.s:
kare dadhānaṃ devībhyāṃ śliṣṭaṃ saṃcintayedvibhum /
lakṣaṃ japo daśāṃśena juhuyātpāyasena tu //
1.81.d:
करे दधानं देवीभ्यां श्लिष्टं संचिन्तयेद्विभुम् ।
लक्षं जपो दशांशेन जुहुयात्पायसेन तु ॥
1.81.m: and a golden cane in his left hand, embraced by his two goddesses. / The recitation is one hundred thousand times; one should offer a tenth of that in fire oblations with milk-rice.

1.81.s:
etābhyāṃ siddhamantrābhyāṃ mantrī kuryādyathepsitam /
praṇavaḥ kamalā māyā namo bhagavate tataḥ //
1.81.d:
एताभ्यां सिद्धमन्त्राभ्यां मन्त्री कुर्याद्यथेप्सितम् ।
प्रणवः कमला माया नमो भगवते ततः ॥
1.81.m: With these two perfected mantras, the mantrin may accomplish whatever he desires. / The praṇava, Kamalā, Māyā, then 'namo bhagavate',

1.81.s:
nandaputrāya tatpaścādbālānte vapuṣe padam /
ūnaviṃśativarṇo 'yaṃ munirbrahmā samīritaḥ //
1.81.d:
नन्दपुत्राय तत्पश्चाद्बालान्ते वपुषे पदम् ।
ऊनविंशतिवर्णो ऽयं मुनिर्ब्रह्मा समीरितः ॥
1.81.m: next 'nandaputrāya', and then the word 'bālavapuṣe'. / This is a nineteen-syllable [mantra]; its seer is declared to be Brahmā;

1.81.s:
chando 'nuṣṭup devatā ca kṛṣṇo bālavapuḥ svayam /
mantro 'yaṃ sarvasaṃpattisiddhaye sevyate budhaiḥ //
1.81.d:
छन्दो ऽनुष्टुप् देवता च कृष्णो बालवपुः स्वयम् ।
मन्त्रो ऽयं सर्वसंपत्तिसिद्धये सेव्यते बुधैः ॥
1.81.m: the metre is anuṣṭubh, and the deity is Kṛṣṇa himself in the form of a child. / This mantra is cultivated by the wise for the attainment of all prosperity.

1.81.s:
tāro hyadbhagavānaṅeṃto rukmiṇīvallabhāya ca /
vahnijāyāvadhiḥ prokto mantraḥ ṣoḍaśavarṇavān //
1.81.d:
तारो ह्यद्भगवानङेंतो रुक्मिणीवल्लभाय च ।
वह्निजायावधिः प्रोक्तो मन्त्रः षोडशवर्णवान् ॥
1.81.m: The praṇava, the heart-mantra, 'bhagavate' ending in the dative, and 'rukmiṇīvallabhāya', / ending with the wife of fire: this is declared to be a sixteen-syllable mantra.

1.81.s:
nārado 'sya muniśchando 'nuṣṭup ca devatā manoḥ /
rukmiṇīvallabhaścandradṛgvedāṅgākṣivarṇakaiḥ /
pañcāṅgāni prakurvīta tato dhyāyetsureśvaram //
1.81.d:
नारदो ऽस्य मुनिश्छन्दो ऽनुष्टुप् च देवता मनोः ।
रुक्मिणीवल्लभश्चन्द्रदृग्वेदाङ्गाक्षिवर्णकैः ।
पञ्चाङ्गानि प्रकुर्वीत ततो ध्यायेत्सुरेश्वरम् ॥
1.81.m: Nārada is its seer, the metre is anuṣṭubh, and the deity of the mantra / is the lover of Rukmiṇī. With one, two, four, six, and two syllables / one should perform the five limbs, and then meditate upon the Lord of gods:

1.81.s:
tāpicchacchaviraṅkagāṃ priyatamāṃ svarṇaprabhāmaṃbujaprodyaddāmabhujāṃ svavāmabhujayāśliṣyansvacittāśayā /
śliṣyantīṃ svayamanyahastavilatsauvarṇavetraściraṃ pāyānnaḥ suviśuddhapītavasano nānāvibhūṣo hariḥ //
1.81.d:
तापिच्छच्छविरङ्कगां प्रियतमां स्वर्णप्रभामंबुजप्रोद्यद्दामभुजां स्ववामभुजयाश्लिष्यन्स्वचित्ताशया ।
श्लिष्यन्तीं स्वयमन्यहस्तविलत्सौवर्णवेत्रश्चिरं पायान्नः सुविशुद्धपीतवसनो नानाविभूषो हरिः ॥
1.81.m: 'Embracing with his left arm his beloved, sitting on his lap, who shines like gold and has arms like blooming lotus vines, / as she embraces him with loving heart, holding in his other hand a glittering golden reed, / dressed in purest yellow garments, adorned with diverse ornaments—may Hari protect us forever!'

1.81.s: dhyātvaivaṃ prajapellakṣaṃ raktaiḥ padmairdaśāṃśataḥ //
1.81.d: ध्यात्वैवं प्रजपेल्लक्षं रक्तैः पद्मैर्दशांशतः ॥
1.81.m: Meditating thus, one should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times, and offer a tenth of that in fire oblations with red lotuses

1.81.s:
trimadhvaktairhunetpīṭhe pūrvokte pūjayeddharim /
aṅgairnāradamukhyaiśca lokeśaiśca tadāyudhaiḥ //
1.81.d:
त्रिमध्वक्तैर्हुनेत्पीठे पूर्वोक्ते पूजयेद्धरिम् ।
अङ्गैर्नारदमुख्यैश्च लोकेशैश्च तदायुधैः ॥
1.81.m: smeared with the three sweets, and worship Hari on the previously described ritual seat, / with the limbs, Nārada and the other [sages], the world-rulers, and their weapons.

1.81.s:
evaṃ siddho manurdadyātsarvānkāmāṃśca mantriṇe /
līlādaṇḍapadābjo 'pi janasaṃsaktadoḥ padam //
1.81.d:
एवं सिद्धो मनुर्दद्यात्सर्वान्कामांश्च मन्त्रिणे ।
लीलादण्डपदाब्जो ऽपि जनसंसक्तदोः पदम् ॥
1.81.m: The mantra thus perfected bestows all desires upon the practitioner. / 'līlādaṇḍapadābjo 'pi janasaṃsaktadoḥpadaṃ',

1.81.s:
daṇḍānte vā dharāvahniradhīśāḍhyo 'tha lohitaḥ /
meghaśyāmapadaṃ paścādbhagavān salilaṃsadṛk //
1.81.d:
दण्डान्ते वा धरावह्निरधीशाढ्यो ऽथ लोहितः ।
मेघश्यामपदं पश्चाद्भगवान् सलिलंसदृक् ॥
1.81.m: or with 'daṇḍa' at the end, earth, fire with its ruler, then the red one, / next the word 'meghaśyāma', 'bhagavān', water with the eye-letter,

1.81.s:
viṣṇo ityuktvā ṭhadvayaṃ syādekonatriṃśadarṇavān /
nārado 'sya muniśchando 'nuṣṭup ca devatā manoḥ //
1.81.d:
विष्णो इत्युक्त्वा ठद्वयं स्यादेकोनत्रिंशदर्णवान् ।
नारदो ऽस्य मुनिश्छन्दो ऽनुष्टुप् च देवता मनोः ॥
1.81.m: and uttering 'viṣṇo', there should be two 'ṭha's: this forms a twenty-nine-syllable mantra. / Nārada is its seer, the metre is anuṣṭubh, and the deity of the mantra

1.81.s:
līlādaṇḍahariḥ prokto manvabdhadhiyugavahnibhiḥ /
vedaiḥ pañcāṃ gakaṃ bhāgairmantravarṇotthitaiḥ kramāt //
1.81.d:
लीलादण्डहरिः प्रोक्तो मन्वब्धधियुगवह्निभिः ।
वेदैः पञ्चां गकं भागैर्मन्त्रवर्णोत्थितैः क्रमात् ॥
1.81.m: is declared to be Līlādaṇḍahari. With fourteen, four, two, three, / and four syllables drawn from the syllables of the mantra in sequence, the five limbs [are performed].

1.81.s:
saṃmohayaṃśca nijavāmakarasthalīlādaṇḍena gopayuvatīḥ parasuṃdarīśca /
diśyannijapriyasakhāṃsagandakṣahasto devaśriyaṃ nihatakaṃsa urukramo naḥ //
1.81.d:
संमोहयंश्च निजवामकरस्थलीलादण्डेन गोपयुवतीः परसुंदरीश्च ।
दिश्यन्निजप्रियसखांसगन्दक्षहस्तो देवश्रियं निहतकंस उरुक्रमो नः ॥
1.81.m: 'Fascinating the young cowherd women and other beautiful maidens with the playful cane in his left hand, / his right hand resting upon the shoulder of his dear companion, having slain Kaṃsa, the wide-striding Lord—may he bestow fortune upon us.'

1.81.s:
lakṣaṃ japo daśāṃśena juhuyāttilataṇḍulaiḥ /
trimadhvaktaistato 'bhyarcedaṅgaṃ dikpālahetibhiḥ //
1.81.d:
लक्षं जपो दशांशेन जुहुयात्तिलतण्डुलैः ।
त्रिमध्वक्तैस्ततो ऽभ्यर्चेदङ्गं दिक्पालहेतिभिः ॥
1.81.m: Recitation is one hundred thousand times; one should offer a tenth of that in fire oblations with sesame and rice grains / smeared with the three sweets; then one should worship the limbs, the guardians of the directions, and their weapons.

1.81.s:
līlādaṇḍa hariṃ yo vai bhajate nityamādarāt /
sa sarvaiḥ pūjyate lokaistasya gehe sthirā ramā //
1.81.d:
लीलादण्ड हरिं यो वै भजते नित्यमादरात् ।
स सर्वैः पूज्यते लोकैस्तस्य गेहे स्थिरा रमा ॥
1.81.m: Whoever constantly and respectfully worships Līlādaṇḍahari / is honoured by all people, and Lakṣmī remains steady in his home.

1.81.s:
sadyārūḍhā smṛtistoyaṃ keśavāḍhyadharāyugam /
bhayāgnivallabhāmantraḥ saptārṇaḥ sarvasiddhidaḥ //
1.81.d:
सद्यारूढा स्मृतिस्तोयं केशवाढ्यधरायुगम् ।
भयाग्निवल्लभामन्त्रः सप्तार्णः सर्वसिद्धिदः ॥
1.81.m: The instant-mounted memory, water, a pair of earth syllables with Keśava, / and the wife of the fear-fire: this is a seven-syllable mantra bestowing all perfections.

1.81.s:
ṛṣiḥ syānnāradaśchando uṣṇiggovallamasya tu /
devatāpūrvavaccakraiḥ pañcāṅgāni tu kalpayet //
1.81.d:
ऋषिः स्यान्नारदश्छन्दो उष्णिग्गोवल्लमस्य तु ।
देवतापूर्ववच्चक्रैः पञ्चाङ्गानि तु कल्पयेत् ॥
1.81.m: Its seer is Nārada, its metre is uṣṇih, and its deity is Govallabha. / As before, one should arrange the five limbs with the disc-syllables.

1.81.s:
dhyeyo hariḥ sakapilāgaṇamadhyasaṃsthastā āhvayandadhaddakṣiṇadosthaveṇum /
pāśaṃ sayaṣṭimaparatra payodanīlaḥ pītāmbarāhiripupicchakṛtāvataṃsaḥ //
1.81.d:
ध्येयो हरिः सकपिलागणमध्यसंस्थस्ता आह्वयन्दधद्दक्षिणदोस्थवेणुम् ।
पाशं सयष्टिमपरत्र पयोदनीलः पीताम्बराहिरिपुपिच्छकृतावतंसः ॥
1.81.m: 'Hari is to be meditated upon standing amid a herd of tawny cows, calling them, holding a flute in his right hand, / a noose with a staff in the other, dark as a raincloud, clad in yellow garments, with a crest-ornament made of peacock feathers.'

1.81.s:
saptalakṣaṃ japenmantraṃ daśāṃśaṃ juhuyāttataḥ /
godugdhaiḥ pūjayetpīṭhe syādaṅgaiḥ prathamāvṛtiḥ //
1.81.d:
सप्तलक्षं जपेन्मन्त्रं दशांशं जुहुयात्ततः ।
गोदुग्धैः पूजयेत्पीठे स्यादङ्गैः प्रथमावृतिः ॥
1.81.m: One should recite the mantra seven hundred thousand times, and then offer a tenth of that in fire oblations / with cow's milk; one should worship him on the ritual seat, the first circuit being the limbs;

1.81.s:
suvarṇapiṅgalāṃ gaurapiṅgalāṃ raktapiṅgalām /
guḍapiṅgāṃ babhruvarṇāṃ cottamāṃ kapilāṃ tathā //
1.81.d:
सुवर्णपिङ्गलां गौरपिङ्गलां रक्तपिङ्गलाम् ।
गुडपिङ्गां बभ्रुवर्णां चोत्तमां कपिलां तथा ॥
1.81.m: worshipping the golden-tawny, the white-tawny, the red-tawny, / the molasses-tawny, the brownish-red, the excellent tawny,

1.81.s:
catuṣkapiṅgalāṃ pītapiṅgalāṃ cottamāṃ śubhām /
gogaṇāṣṭakamabhyarcya lokeśānuyudhairyutān //
1.81.d:
चतुष्कपिङ्गलां पीतपिङ्गलां चोत्तमां शुभाम् ।
गोगणाष्टकमभ्यर्च्य लोकेशानुयुधैर्युतान् ॥
1.81.m: the four-legged tawny, and the auspicious excellent yellow-tawny— / having worshipped this group of eight cows and the world-rulers endowed with their weapons,

1.81.s:
saṃpūjyaivaṃ manau siddhe kuryātkāmyāni mantravit /
aṣṭottarasahasraṃ yaḥ payobhirdinaśo hunet //
1.81.d:
संपूज्यैवं मनौ सिद्धे कुर्यात्काम्यानि मन्त्रवित् ।
अष्टोत्तरसहस्रं यः पयोभिर्दिनशो हुनेत् ॥
1.81.m: and having thus worshipped, when the mantra is perfected, the knower of mantras should perform desired rites. / He who offers oblations of milk one thousand and eight times daily

1.81.s:
pakṣātsagogaṇo mukto daśārṇe cāpyayaṃ vidhiḥ /
tāro hṛdbhagavān ṅeṃtaḥ śrīgovindastathā bhavet //
1.81.d:
पक्षात्सगोगणो मुक्तो दशार्णे चाप्ययं विधिः ।
तारो हृद्भगवान् ङेंतः श्रीगोविन्दस्तथा भवेत् ॥
1.81.m: for a fortnight is freed along with his herds of cattle. This procedure applies also to the ten-syllable [mantra]. / The praṇava, the heart-mantra, 'bhagavate' ending in the dative, and then 'śrīgovindāya'—

1.81.s:
dvādaśārṇo manuḥ prokto nārado 'sya munirmataḥ /
chandaḥ proktaṃ ca gāyatrī śrīgovindo 'sya devatā /
candrākṣiyugabhūtārṇaiḥ sarvaiḥ pañcāṅgakalpanam //
1.81.d:
द्वादशार्णो मनुः प्रोक्तो नारदो ऽस्य मुनिर्मतः ।
छन्दः प्रोक्तं च गायत्री श्रीगोविन्दो ऽस्य देवता ।
चन्द्राक्षियुगभूतार्णैः सर्वैः पञ्चाङ्गकल्पनम् ॥
1.81.m: this is declared to be a twelve-syllable mantra; Nārada is considered its seer, / the metre is declared to be gāyatrī, and Śrīgovinda is its deity; / the arrangement of the five limbs is made with one, two, four, five, and all the syllables.

1.81.s: dhyāyetkalpadrumūlāśritamaṇivilasaddivyasiṃhāsanasthaṃ meghaśyāmaṃ piśaṅgāṃśukamatisubhagaṃ śaṅkharetre karābhyām //
1.81.d: ध्यायेत्कल्पद्रुमूलाश्रितमणिविलसद्दिव्यसिंहासनस्थं मेघश्यामं पिशङ्गांशुकमतिसुभगं शङ्खरेत्रे कराभ्याम् ॥
1.81.m: 'One should meditate on him seated upon a divine throne shining with gems at the base of the wish-fulfilling tree, / dark as a raincloud, wearing yellowish garments, exceedingly charming, holding a conch and a cane with his hands,

1.81.s: bibhrāṇaṃ gosahasrairvṛtamamarapatiṃ prauḍhahastaikakuṃbhapraścotatsaudhadhārāsnapitamabhinavāṃbhojapatrābhanetram //
1.81.d: बिभ्राणं गोसहस्रैर्वृतममरपतिं प्रौढहस्तैककुंभप्रश्चोतत्सौधधारास्नपितमभिनवांभोजपत्राभनेत्रम् ॥
1.81.m: surrounded by thousands of cows, the Lord of the immortals, bathed by streams of nectar dripping from a single jar held in his mature hand, his eyes resembling the petals of a fresh lotus.'

1.81.s:
ravilakṣaṃ japenmantraṃ dugdhairhutvā daśāṃśataḥ /
yajecca pūrvavadgoṣṭhasthitaṃ vā pratimādiṣu //
1.81.d:
रविलक्षं जपेन्मन्त्रं दुग्धैर्हुत्वा दशांशतः ।
यजेच्च पूर्ववद्गोष्ठस्थितं वा प्रतिमादिषु ॥
1.81.m: One should recite the mantra one million two hundred thousand times, offer a tenth of that in fire oblations with milk, / and worship as before in a cowshed or in images and the like.

1.81.s:
pūrvokte vaiṣṇave pīṭhe mūrtiṃ saṃkalpya mūlataḥ /
tatrāvāhya yajetkṛṣṇaṃ gurupūjanapūrvakam //
1.81.d:
पूर्वोक्ते वैष्णवे पीठे मूर्तिं संकल्प्य मूलतः ।
तत्रावाह्य यजेत्कृष्णं गुरुपूजनपूर्वकम् ॥
1.81.m: Having conceived the icon from the root-mantra on the previously described Vaiṣṇava ritual seat, / having invoked Kṛṣṇa there, one should worship him, preceded by worship of the guru.

1.81.s:
rukmiṇīṃ satyabhāmāṃ ca pārśvayorindramagrataḥ /
pṛṣṭhataḥ surabhiṃ ceṣṭvā kesareṣvaṅgapūjanam //
1.81.d:
रुक्मिणीं सत्यभामां च पार्श्वयोरिन्द्रमग्रतः ।
पृष्ठतः सुरभिं चेष्ट्वा केसरेष्वङ्गपूजनम् ॥
1.81.m: Having worshipped Rukmiṇī and Satyabhāmā on the two flanks, Indra in front, / and Surabhi behind, [there is] the worship of the limbs upon the filaments.

1.81.s:
kāliṃ dyādyā mahiṣyo 'ṣṭau vasupatreṣu saṃsthitāḥ /
pīṭhakoṇeṣu baddhvādikiṅkaṇīṃ ca tathā punaḥ //
1.81.d:
कालिं द्याद्या महिष्यो ऽष्टौ वसुपत्रेषु संस्थिताः ।
पीठकोणेषु बद्ध्वादिकिङ्कणीं च तथा पुनः ॥
1.81.m: Kālindī and the other eight chief queens reside on the eight petals; / having bound [the cords] in the corners of the seat, and likewise bells,

1.81.s:
dāmāni pṛṣṭhayorveṇuṃ puraḥ śrīvatsakaustubhau /
agrato vanamāsādirdikṣvaṣṭasu tathā sthitāḥ //
1.81.d:
दामानि पृष्ठयोर्वेणुं पुरः श्रीवत्सकौस्तुभौ ।
अग्रतो वनमासादिर्दिक्ष्वष्टसु तथा स्थिताः ॥
1.81.m: ropes behind, the flute in front, and Śrīvatsa and Kaustubha in front; / the garland of wild flowers and others are positioned ahead in the eight directions,

1.81.s:
pāñcajanyaṃ gadā cakraṃ vasudevaśca devakī /
nandagopo yaśodā ca sagogopālagopikāḥ //
1.81.d:
पाञ्चजन्यं गदा चक्रं वसुदेवश्च देवकी ।
नन्दगोपो यशोदा च सगोगोपालगोपिकाः ॥
1.81.m: as well as Pāñcajanya, the mace, the discus, Vasudeva, and Devakī, / Nandagopa, Yaśodā, together with the cattle, cowherds, and cowherd women.

1.81.s:
indrādyāśca sthitā bāhye vajrādyāśca tataḥ param /
kumudaḥ kumudākṣaśca puṇḍarīko 'tha vāmanaḥ //
1.81.d:
इन्द्राद्याश्च स्थिता बाह्ये वज्राद्याश्च ततः परम् ।
कुमुदः कुमुदाक्षश्च पुण्डरीको ऽथ वामनः ॥
1.81.m: Indra and the others are situated outside, and after them the thunderbolt and the other [weapons]. / Kumuda, Kumudākṣa, Puṇḍarīka, then Vāmana,

1.81.s:
śaṅkukarṇaḥ sarvanetraḥ sumukhaḥ supratiṣṭitaḥ /
viṣvaksenaśca saṃpūjyaḥ svātmā cārcyastataḥ param //
1.81.d:
शङ्कुकर्णः सर्वनेत्रः सुमुखः सुप्रतिष्टितः ।
विष्वक्सेनश्च संपूज्यः स्वात्मा चार्च्यस्ततः परम् ॥
1.81.m: Śaṅkukarṇa, Sarvanetra, Sumukha, Supratiṣṭhita, / and Viṣvaksena are to be worshipped; and after that, one's own self is to be worshipped.

1.81.s:
ekakālaṃ trikālaṃ vā yo govindaṃ yajennaraḥ /
sa cirāyurnirātaṅko dhanadhānyapatirbhavet //
1.81.d:
एककालं त्रिकालं वा यो गोविन्दं यजेन्नरः ।
स चिरायुर्निरातङ्को धनधान्यपतिर्भवेत् ॥
1.81.m: The person who worships Govinda once a day or at the three junctions of the day / will have a long life, be free from illness, and become a master of wealth and grain.

1.81.s:
smṛtiḥ sadyānvitā cakrī dakṣakarṇayutodharā /
nāthāya hṛdayānto 'yaṃ vasuvarṇo mahāmanuḥ //
1.81.d:
स्मृतिः सद्यान्विता चक्री दक्षकर्णयुतोधरा ।
नाथाय हृदयान्तो ऽयं वसुवर्णो महामनुः ॥
1.81.m: The Smṛti [letter] joined with Sadya, the discus-bearer, the earth letter joined with the right ear, / followed by 'to the Lord' and ending with Hṛdaya—this is the eight-syllable great mantra.

1.81.s:
munirbrahmāsya gāyatrī chandaḥ kṛṣṇo 'sya devatā /
varṇadvandvaiśca sarveṇa pañcāṅgānyasya kalpayet //
1.81.d:
मुनिर्ब्रह्मास्य गायत्री छन्दः कृष्णो ऽस्य देवता ।
वर्णद्वन्द्वैश्च सर्वेण पञ्चाङ्गान्यस्य कल्पयेत् ॥
1.81.m: Its sage is Brahmā, its meter is gāyatrī, and its deity is Kṛṣṇa. / With pairs of syllables and with the whole, one should fashion its five limbs.

1.81.s:
pañcavarṣamatilolamaṅgaṇe dhāvamānamaticañcalekṣaṇam /
kiṅkiṇīvalayahāranūpurai rañjitaṃ namata gopabālakam //
1.81.d:
पञ्चवर्षमतिलोलमङ्गणे धावमानमतिचञ्चलेक्षणम् ।
किङ्किणीवलयहारनूपुरै रञ्जितं नमत गोपबालकम् ॥
1.81.m: Bow to the cowherd child, five years of age, very playful, running in the courtyard, / with very restless eyes, adorned with bells, bracelets, necklaces, and anklets.

1.81.s:
evaṃ dhyātvā japedaṣṭalakṣaṃ mantrī daśāṃśataḥ /
brahmavṛkṣasamidbhiśca juhuyātpāyasena vā //
1.81.d:
एवं ध्यात्वा जपेदष्टलक्षं मन्त्री दशांशतः ।
ब्रह्मवृक्षसमिद्भिश्च जुहुयात्पायसेन वा ॥
1.81.m: Having meditated thus, the practitioner should recite it eight hundred thousand times, / and should make fire oblations for a tenth of that with kindling sticks of the Brahma tree or with milk-rice.

1.81.s:
prāgukte vaiṣṇave pīṭhe mūrtiṃ saṃkalpya mūlataḥ /
tatrāvāhyārcayetkṛṣṇaṃ mantrī vai sthiramānasaḥ //
1.81.d:
प्रागुक्ते वैष्णवे पीठे मूर्तिं संकल्प्य मूलतः ।
तत्रावाह्यार्चयेत्कृष्णं मन्त्री वै स्थिरमानसः ॥
1.81.m: Having fashioned the form upon the previously mentioned Vaiṣṇava seat with the basic mantra, / the practitioner, with a steady mind, should invoke and worship Kṛṣṇa there.

1.81.s:
kesareṣu caturdikṣu vidikṣvaṅgāni pūjayet /
vāsudevaṃ balaṃ dikṣu pradyumnamaniruddhakam //
1.81.d:
केसरेषु चतुर्दिक्षु विदिक्ष्वङ्गानि पूजयेत् ।
वासुदेवं बलं दिक्षु प्रद्युम्नमनिरुद्धकम् ॥
1.81.m: Upon the filaments, he should worship the limbs in the four cardinal and intermediate directions; / in the cardinal directions, Vāsudeva, Bala, Pradyumna, and Aniruddha;

1.81.s:
vidikṣu rukmiṇīsatyabhāme vai lakṣyaṇarkṣaje /
lokeśānsāyudhānbāhye evaṃ siddho bhavenmanuḥ //
1.81.d:
विदिक्षु रुक्मिणीसत्यभामे वै लक्ष्यणर्क्षजे ।
लोकेशान्सायुधान्बाह्ये एवं सिद्धो भवेन्मनुः ॥
1.81.m: in the intermediate directions, Rukmiṇī, Satyabhāmā, Lakṣmaṇā, and the daughter of the bear; / and outside, the guardians of the world with their weapons. Thus the mantra becomes perfected.

1.81.s:
tāraḥ śrībhuvanākāmo ṅeṃtaṃ śrīkṛṣṇamīrayet /
śrīgovindaṃ tataḥ procya gopījanapadaṃ tataḥ //
1.81.d:
तारः श्रीभुवनाकामो ङेंतं श्रीकृष्णमीरयेत् ।
श्रीगोविन्दं ततः प्रोच्य गोपीजनपदं ततः ॥
1.81.m: One should utter the Pranava, Śrī, Bhuvana, and Kāma; Śrīkṛṣṇa in the dative; / then having spoken Śrīgovinda; then the word Gopījana;

1.81.s:
vallabhāya tataḥ padmātrayaṃ tatvākṣaro manuḥ /
munyādikaṃ ca pūrvoktaṃ siddhagopālakaṃ smaret //
1.81.d:
वल्लभाय ततः पद्मात्रयं तत्वाक्षरो मनुः ।
मुन्यादिकं च पूर्वोक्तं सिद्धगोपालकं स्मरेत् ॥
1.81.m: then 'to the beloved' [Vallabhāya]; and three times Padmā—this is the twenty-five-syllable mantra. / The sage and the rest are as stated before; one should remember the perfected Gopāla:

1.81.s:
mādhavīmaṇḍapāsīnau garuḍenābhipālitau /
divyakrīḍāsu niratau rāmakṛṣṇau smaran japet //
1.81.d:
माधवीमण्डपासीनौ गरुडेनाभिपालितौ ।
दिव्यक्रीडासु निरतौ रामकृष्णौ स्मरन् जपेत् ॥
1.81.m: Seated in a bower of spring creepers, protected by Garuḍa, / engrossed in divine sports—remembering Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, one should recite.

1.81.s:
pūjanaṃ pūrvavaccāsya kartavyaṃ vaiṣṇavottamaiḥ /
cakrī munisvaropetaḥ sargī caikākṣaro manuḥ //
1.81.d:
पूजनं पूर्ववच्चास्य कर्तव्यं वैष्णवोत्तमैः ।
चक्री मुनिस्वरोपेतः सर्गी चैकाक्षरो मनुः ॥
1.81.m: Its worship should be performed as before by the best of Vaiṣṇavas. / The discus-bearer endowed with the seventh vowel and with the visarga is the single-syllable mantra.

1.81.s:
kṛṣṇeti dvyakṣaraḥ proktaḥ kāmādiḥ syāttrivarṇakaḥ /
saiva ṅeṃto yugārṇaḥ syātkṛṣṇāya nama ityapi //
1.81.d:
कृष्णेति द्व्यक्षरः प्रोक्तः कामादिः स्यात्त्रिवर्णकः ।
सैव ङेंतो युगार्णः स्यात्कृष्णाय नम इत्यपि ॥
1.81.m: The two-syllabled [mantra] is taught as 'Kṛṣṇa'; with the Kāma-bīja first, it becomes three syllables. / That very [mantra] ending in the dative is four syllables, namely 'Kṛṣṇāya namaḥ'.

1.81.s:
pañcākṣaraśca kṛṣṇāya kāmaruddhastathā paraḥ /
gopālāyāgnijāyānto rasavarṇaḥ prakīrtitaḥ //
1.81.d:
पञ्चाक्षरश्च कृष्णाय कामरुद्धस्तथा परः ।
गोपालायाग्निजायान्तो रसवर्णः प्रकीर्तितः ॥
1.81.m: And the five-syllabled one is 'Kṛṣṇāya' enclosed by Kāma; likewise another / ending in the wife of Agni [svāhā] is 'Gopālāya', proclaimed to have six syllables.

1.81.s:
kāmaḥ kṛṣṇapadaṃ ṅeṃtaṃ vahnijāyāntakaḥ paraḥ /
kṛṣṇagovindakau ṅeṃtau saptārṇaḥ sarvasiddhidaḥ //
1.81.d:
कामः कृष्णपदं ङेंतं वह्निजायान्तकः परः ।
कृष्णगोविन्दकौ ङेंतौ सप्तार्णः सर्वसिद्धिदः ॥
1.81.m: Kāma, the word 'Kṛṣṇa' in the dative, and ending in the wife of Agni [svāhā] is another; / 'Kṛṣṇa' and 'Govinda' in the dative is the seven-syllabled one that grants all perfections.

1.81.s:
śrīśaktikāmāḥ kṛṣṇāya kāmaḥ saptākṣaraḥ paraḥ /
kṛṣṇagovindakau ṅeṃtau hṛdanto 'nyo navākṣaraḥ //
1.81.d:
श्रीशक्तिकामाः कृष्णाय कामः सप्ताक्षरः परः ।
कृष्णगोविन्दकौ ङेंतौ हृदन्तो ऽन्यो नवाक्षरः ॥
1.81.m: Śrī, Śakti, and Kāma [bījas], then 'Kṛṣṇāya' and Kāma, is another seven-syllabled one; / 'Kṛṣṇa' and 'Govinda' in the dative, ending in 'hṛd' [namaḥ], is another, nine-syllabled one.

1.81.s:
ṅeṃtau ca kṛṣṇagovindau tathā kāmaḥ puṭaḥ paraḥ /
kāmaḥ śārṅgī dharāsaṃstho manvindvāḍhyaśca manmathaḥ //
1.81.d:
ङेंतौ च कृष्णगोविन्दौ तथा कामः पुटः परः ।
कामः शार्ङ्गी धरासंस्थो मन्विन्द्वाढ्यश्च मन्मथः ॥
1.81.m: And 'Kṛṣṇa' and 'Govinda' in the dative, enclosed likewise by Kāma, is another; / Kāma, the bearer of Śārṅga with the vowel 'u', endowed with bindu, and Kāma [i.e., klīṃ klūṃ klīṃ],

1.81.s:
śyāmalāṅgāya hṛdayaṃ daśārṇaḥ sarvasiddhidaḥ /
bālānte vapuṣe kṛṣṇāyāgnijāyāntimo 'paraḥ //
1.81.d:
श्यामलाङ्गाय हृदयं दशार्णः सर्वसिद्धिदः ।
बालान्ते वपुषे कृष्णायाग्निजायान्तिमो ऽपरः ॥
1.81.m: followed by 'Śyāmalāṅgāya hṛdayam' [namaḥ], is the ten-syllabled one that grants all perfections; / another ends in the wife of Agni [svāhā]: 'Bāla' followed by 'vapuṣe kṛṣṇāya'.

1.81.s:
dviṭhānte bālavapuṣe kāmaḥ kṛṣṇāya saṃvadet /
tato dhyāyansvahṛdaye gopījanamanoharam //
1.81.d:
द्विठान्ते बालवपुषे कामः कृष्णाय संवदेत् ।
ततो ध्यायन्स्वहृदये गोपीजनमनोहरम् ॥
1.81.m: Ending in dviṭhā [svāhā], one should utter Kāma, 'Kṛṣṇāya bālavapuṣe'; / then, meditating in one's heart on the captivator of the gopīs' hearts:

1.81.s:
śrīvṛndāvipinapratoliṣu namatsaṃphullavallītatiṣvantarjālavighaṭṭainaḥ surabhiṇā vātena saṃsevite /
kālindīpuline vihāriṇamatho rādhaikajīvātukaṃ vande nandakiśoraminduvadanaṃ snigdhāṃbudāḍaṃbaram //
1.81.d:
श्रीवृन्दाविपिनप्रतोलिषु नमत्संफुल्लवल्लीततिष्वन्तर्जालविघट्टैनः सुरभिणा वातेन संसेविते ।
कालिन्दीपुलिने विहारिणमथो राधैकजीवातुकं वन्दे नन्दकिशोरमिन्दुवदनं स्निग्धांबुदाडंबरम् ॥
1.81.m: "I praise the youthful son of Nanda, whose face is like the moon, who displays the grace of a glossy cloud, / who sports on the sandbanks of the Kālindī, the sole life of Rādhā, / served by the fragrant breeze charged with drops of water / in the lanes of the forest of glorious Vṛndā, where clusters of blossoms bend low."

1.81.s:
pūrvāktavartmanā pūjā jñeyā hyeṣāṃ munīśvara /
devakīsutavarṇānte govindapadamuccaret //
1.81.d:
पूर्वाक्तवर्त्मना पूजा ज्ञेया ह्येषां मुनीश्वर ।
देवकीसुतवर्णान्ते गोविन्दपदमुच्चरेत् ॥
1.81.m: Their worship is to be understood as performed by the previously mentioned method, O lord of sages. / Following the syllables 'Devakīsuta', one should utter the word 'Govinda',

1.81.s:
vāsudevapadaṃ procya saṃbṛddhyantaṃ jagatpatiṃm /
dehi me tanayaṃ paścātkṛṣṇa tvāmahamīrayet //
1.81.d:
वासुदेवपदं प्रोच्य संबृद्ध्यन्तं जगत्पतिंम् ।
देहि मे तनयं पश्चात्कृष्ण त्वामहमीरयेत् ॥
1.81.m: and having spoken the word 'Vāsudeva' in the vocative, one should say 'Jagatpatim, / dehi me tanayaṃ', and thereafter 'Kṛṣṇa tvām aham

1.81.s:
śaraṇaṃ gata ityanto mantro dvātriṃśadakṣaraḥ /
nārado 'sya muniśchando gāyatrī cāpyanuṣṭubham /
devaḥ sutapradaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ pādaiḥ sarveṇa cāṅgakam //
1.81.d:
शरणं गत इत्यन्तो मन्त्रो द्वात्रिंशदक्षरः ।
नारदो ऽस्य मुनिश्छन्दो गायत्री चाप्यनुष्टुभम् ।
देवः सुतप्रदः कृष्णः पादैः सर्वेण चाङ्गकम् ॥
1.81.m: śaraṇaṃ gataḥ'; this is the thirty-two-syllabled mantra. / Its sage is Nārada, the metre is gāyatrī and anuṣṭubh, / the deity is Kṛṣṇa who grants sons, and the limb-placement is performed with each quarter and with the whole [mantra].

1.81.s:
vijayena yuto rathasthitaḥ prasamānīya samudramadhyataḥ /
pradadattanayān dvijanmane smaraṇīyo vasudevanandanaḥ //
1.81.d:
विजयेन युतो रथस्थितः प्रसमानीय समुद्रमध्यतः ।
प्रददत्तनयान् द्विजन्मने स्मरणीयो वसुदेवनन्दनः ॥
1.81.m: Accompanied by Arjuna, mounted upon a chariot, having brought back by force from the midst of the ocean / and returned the sons to the twice-born sage—thus is the son of Vasudeva to be remembered.

1.81.s:
lakṣaṃ japo 'yutaṃ homastalairmadhurasaṃplutaiḥ /
arcā pūrvodite pīṭhe aṅgalokeśvarāyudhaiḥ //
1.81.d:
लक्षं जपो ऽयुतं होमस्तलैर्मधुरसंप्लुतैः ।
अर्चा पूर्वोदिते पीठे अङ्गलोकेश्वरायुधैः ॥
1.81.m: One hundred thousand recitations, ten thousand fire oblations with sesamum seeds bathed in sweet liquids, / and worship upon the previously described ritual seat, with the limbs, the lords of the quarters, and their weapons.

1.81.s:
evaṃ siddhe manau mantrī vandhyāyāmapi putravān /
tāro māyā tataḥ sāṃtaseṃduṣvāntaśca sarvavān //
1.81.d:
एवं सिद्धे मनौ मन्त्री वन्ध्यायामपि पुत्रवान् ।
तारो माया ततः सांतसेंदुष्वान्तश्च सर्ववान् ॥
1.81.m: When the mantra is thus perfected, the mantra-practitioner obtains a son even from a barren woman. / Tāra [oṃ], māyā [hrīṃ], then 'sa' with bindu, and the end of darkness [ū] endowed with bindu [i.e., sūṃ],

1.81.s:
so 'haṃ vahnipriyānto 'yaṃ mantro vasvakṣaraḥ paraḥ /
pañcabrahmātmakasyāsya mantrasya muni sattamaḥ //
1.81.d:
सो ऽहं वह्निप्रियान्तो ऽयं मन्त्रो वस्वक्षरः परः ।
पञ्चब्रह्मात्मकस्यास्य मन्त्रस्य मुनि सत्तमः ॥
1.81.m: 'so 'ham', ending with the beloved of Agni [svāhā]: this is another, eight-syllabled mantra. / Of this mantra, which consists of the five Brahmans, O best of sages,

1.81.s:
ṛṣirbrahmā ca paramā gāyatrīchanda īritam /
parañjyotiḥ paraṃ brahma devatā parikīrtitam //
1.81.d:
ऋषिर्ब्रह्मा च परमा गायत्रीछन्द ईरितम् ।
परञ्ज्योतिः परं ब्रह्म देवता परिकीर्तितम् ॥
1.81.m: the ṛṣi is Brahmā, the supreme gāyatrī is declared as the metre, / and the deity is proclaimed to be the supreme light, the supreme Brahman.

1.81.s:
praṇavo bījamākhyātaṃ svāhā śaktirudāhṛtā /
svāheti hṛdayaṃ proktaṃ so 'haṃ veti śiro matam //
1.81.d:
प्रणवो बीजमाख्यातं स्वाहा शक्तिरुदाहृता ।
स्वाहेति हृदयं प्रोक्तं सो ऽहं वेति शिरो मतम् ॥
1.81.m: The praṇava is declared as the bīja, svāhā is proclaimed as the śakti; / 'svāhā' is taught as the heart, and 'so 'ham' is regarded as the head;

1.81.s:
haṃsaśceti śikhā proktā hṛllekhā kavacaṃ smṛtam /
praṇavo netramākhyātamastraṃ harihareti ca //
1.81.d:
हंसश्चेति शिखा प्रोक्ता हृल्लेखा कवचं स्मृतम् ।
प्रणवो नेत्रमाख्यातमस्त्रं हरिहरेति च ॥
1.81.m: 'haṃsaḥ' is taught as the crest, and the hṛllekhā [hrīṃ] is considered the armor; / the praṇava is declared as the eye, and the weapon is 'Hari-Hara'.

1.81.s:
sa brahmā sa śivo vipra sa hariḥ saiva devarāṭ /
sa sarvarūpaḥ sarvākhyaḥ so 'kṣaraḥ paramaḥ svarāṭ //
1.81.d:
स ब्रह्मा स शिवो विप्र स हरिः सैव देवराट् ।
स सर्वरूपः सर्वाख्यः सो ऽक्षरः परमः स्वराट् ॥
1.81.m: He is Brahmā, he is Śiva, O twice-born, he is Hari, and he alone is Indra; / he is all-formed, all-named, imperishable, supreme, and self-sovereign.

1.81.s:
evaṃ dhyātvā japedaṣṭalakṣahomo daśāṃśataḥ /
pūjāpraṇavapīṭhe 'sya sāṃgāvaraṇakairmatā //
1.81.d:
एवं ध्यात्वा जपेदष्टलक्षहोमो दशांशतः ।
पूजाप्रणवपीठे ऽस्य सांगावरणकैर्मता ॥
1.81.m: Having thus meditated, one should recite it eight hundred thousand times, with fire oblation of one-tenth; / his worship is regarded as being performed on the praṇava-seat, with the ancillary and surrounding deities.

1.81.s:
evaṃ siddhe manau jñānaṃ sādhakendrasya nārada /
jāyate tattvamasyādivākyoktaṃ nirvikalpakam //
1.81.d:
एवं सिद्धे मनौ ज्ञानं साधकेन्द्रस्य नारद ।
जायते तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्योक्तं निर्विकल्पकम् ॥
1.81.m: When the mantra is thus perfected, O Nārada, there arises in the best of practitioners / the non-conceptual knowledge taught in such statements as 'That thou art'.

1.81.s:
kāmo ṅeṃto hṛṣīkeśo hṛdayānto gajākṣaraḥ /
ṛṣirbrahmāsya gāyatrī chando gāyatramīritam //
1.81.d:
कामो ङेंतो हृषीकेशो हृदयान्तो गजाक्षरः ।
ऋषिर्ब्रह्मास्य गायत्री छन्दो गायत्रमीरितम् ॥
1.81.m: Kāma [klīṃ], 'Hṛṣīkeśa' in the dative, ending in 'hṛdaya' [namaḥ] is the eight-syllabled one; / its ṛṣi is Brahmā, and the metre is declared to be gāyatrī.

1.81.s:
devatā tu hṛṣīkeśo viniyogo 'khilāptaye /
kāmo bījaṃ tathāyeti śaktirasya hyudāhṛtā //
1.81.d:
देवता तु हृषीकेशो विनियोगो ऽखिलाप्तये ।
कामो बीजं तथायेति शक्तिरस्य ह्युदाहृता ॥
1.81.m: The deity is Hṛṣīkeśa, the application is for the attainment of all desires; / Kāma is the bīja, and 'āyā' is declared to be its śakti.

1.81.s:
bījenaiva ṣaḍaṅgāni kṛtvā dhyānaṃ samācaret /
puruṣottamamantroktaṃ sarvaṃ vāsya prakīrtitam //
1.81.d:
बीजेनैव षडङ्गानि कृत्वा ध्यानं समाचरेत् ।
पुरुषोत्तममन्त्रोक्तं सर्वं वास्य प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
1.81.m: Having performed the six limbs with the bīja alone, one should perform meditation; / or everything taught for the Puruṣottama-mantra is proclaimed for it.

1.81.s:
lakṣaṃ japo 'yutaṃ homo ghṛtenaiva prakīrtitaḥ /
tarpaṇaṃ sarvakāmāptyai proktaṃ saṃmohinīsumaiḥ //
1.81.d:
लक्षं जपो ऽयुतं होमो घृतेनैव प्रकीर्तितः ।
तर्पणं सर्वकामाप्त्यै प्रोक्तं संमोहिनीसुमैः ॥
1.81.m: One hundred thousand recitations, and ten thousand fire oblations with ghee alone are proclaimed; / water oblation with saṃmohinī flowers is prescribed for the attainment of all desires.

1.81.s:
śrībījaṃ śaktirāpeti bījenaiva ṣaḍaṅkastathā /
trailokyamohanaḥ śabdo namoṃ'to manurīritaḥ //
1.81.d:
श्रीबीजं शक्तिरापेति बीजेनैव षडङ्कस्तथा ।
त्रैलोक्यमोहनः शब्दो नमोंऽतो मनुरीरितः ॥
1.81.m: The śrī-bīja [śrīṃ], the śakti [hrīṃ], 'āpaḥ', and likewise the six limbs with the bīja itself; / the words 'trailokyamohana' ending in 'namaḥ' is the mantra declared.

1.81.s:
ṛṣirbrahmā ca gāyatrī chandaḥ śrīdharadevatā /
śrībījaṃ śaktirāpeti bījenaiva ṣaḍaṅgakam //
1.81.d:
ऋषिर्ब्रह्मा च गायत्री छन्दः श्रीधरदेवता ।
श्रीबीजं शक्तिरापेति बीजेनैव षडङ्गकम् ॥
1.81.m: The ṛṣi is Brahmā, the metre is gāyatrī, and the deity is Śrīdhara; / the śrī-bīja [śrīṃ] is the bīja, the śakti [hrīṃ], and the six limbs are done with the bīja itself.

1.81.s:
puruṣottamavaddhyānapūjādikamihoditaḥ /
lakṣaṃ japastathā homa ājyenaiva daśāṃśataḥ //
1.81.d:
पुरुषोत्तमवद्ध्यानपूजादिकमिहोदितः ।
लक्षं जपस्तथा होम आज्येनैव दशांशतः ॥
1.81.m: Meditation, worship, and so forth are taught here as for Puruṣottama; / one hundred thousand recitations, and fire oblation of one-tenth of that with ghee alone.

1.81.s:
sugandhaśvetapuṣpaistu pūjāṃ homādikaṃ caret /
evaṃ kṛte tu viprendra sākṣātsyācchrīdharaḥ svayam //
1.81.d:
सुगन्धश्वेतपुष्पैस्तु पूजां होमादिकं चरेत् ।
एवं कृते तु विप्रेन्द्र साक्षात्स्याच्छ्रीधरः स्वयम् ॥
1.81.m: One should perform worship, fire oblation, and so forth with fragrant white flowers; / when this is done, O best of the twice-born, Śrīdhara himself appears visibly.

1.81.s:
acyutānantagovindapadaṃ ṅeṃtaṃ namontimam /
mantro 'sya śaunakaṛṣirvirāṭ chandaḥ prakīrtitam //
1.81.d:
अच्युतानन्तगोविन्दपदं ङेंतं नमोन्तिमम् ।
मन्त्रो ऽस्य शौनकऋषिर्विराट् छन्दः प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
1.81.m: The words 'Acyuta', 'Ananta', and 'Govinda' in the dative, ending in 'namaḥ'— / of this mantra, the sage is Śaunaka, and the metre is proclaimed to be virāṭ.

1.81.s:
eṣāṃ parāśaravyāsanāradā ṛṣayaḥ smṛtāḥ /
virāṭ chandaḥ samākhyātaṃ parabrahmātmako hariḥ //
1.81.d:
एषां पराशरव्यासनारदा ऋषयः स्मृताः ।
विराट् छन्दः समाख्यातं परब्रह्मात्मको हरिः ॥
1.81.m: For these [mantras], Parāśara, Vyāsa, and Nārada are remembered as the sages; / the metre is proclaimed to be virāṭ, and the deity is Hari, whose essence is the supreme Brahman.

1.81.s:
devatābījaśaktī tu pūrvokte sādhakairmate /
śaṅkhacakradharaṃ devaṃ caturbāhuṃ kirīṭinam //
1.81.d:
देवताबीजशक्ती तु पूर्वोक्ते साधकैर्मते ।
शङ्खचक्रधरं देवं चतुर्बाहुं किरीटिनम् ॥
1.81.m: The bīja and śakti are considered by practitioners to be as previously stated. / [One should meditate on] the four-armed God wearing a diadem, holding the conch and disc,

1.81.s:
sarvairapyāyudhairyuktaṃ garuḍopari saṃsthitam /
sanakādimunīndraistu sarvadevairupāsitam //
1.81.d:
सर्वैरप्यायुधैर्युक्तं गरुडोपरि संस्थितम् ।
सनकादिमुनीन्द्रैस्तु सर्वदेवैरुपासितम् ॥
1.81.m: equipped with all weapons, seated upon Garuḍa, / worshipped by the lords of sages beginning with Sanaka and by all the gods,

1.81.s:
śrībhūmisahitaṃ devamudayādityasannibham /
prātarudyatsahasrāṃśumaṇḍalopamakuṇḍalam //
1.81.d:
श्रीभूमिसहितं देवमुदयादित्यसन्निभम् ।
प्रातरुद्यत्सहस्रांशुमण्डलोपमकुण्डलम् ॥
1.81.m: the God accompanied by Śrī and Bhūmi, resembling the rising sun, / whose ear-rings resemble the orb of the thousand-rayed sun rising in the morning,

1.81.s:
sarvalokasya rakṣārthamanantaṃ nityameva hi /
abhayaṃ varadaṃ devaṃ prayacchantaṃ mudānvitam //
1.81.d:
सर्वलोकस्य रक्षार्थमनन्तं नित्यमेव हि ।
अभयं वरदं देवं प्रयच्छन्तं मुदान्वितम् ॥
1.81.m: the eternal Ananta himself, for the protection of all the worlds, / the cheerful God bestowing freedom from fear and boons.

1.81.s:
evaṃ dhyātvār cayetpīṭhe vaiṣṇave susamāhitaḥ /
ādyāvaraṇasaṃgaiḥ syāccakraśaṅkhagadāsibhiḥ //
1.81.d:
एवं ध्यात्वार् चयेत्पीठे वैष्णवे सुसमाहितः ।
आद्यावरणसंगैः स्याच्चक्रशङ्खगदासिभिः ॥
1.81.m: Having thus meditated, well-concentrated, one should worship him upon the Vaiṣṇava ritual seat; / the first surrounding group consists of the disc, conch, mace, and sword;

1.81.s:
muśalāḍhyadhanuḥ pāśāṅkuśaiḥ proktaṃ dvitīyakam /
sanakādikaśākteyavyāsanāradaśaunakaiḥ //
1.81.d:
मुशलाढ्यधनुः पाशाङ्कुशैः प्रोक्तं द्वितीयकम् ।
सनकादिकशाक्तेयव्यासनारदशौनकैः ॥
1.81.m: the second is taught with the pestle, bow, noose, and goad; / the third is proclaimed with the sages beginning with Sanaka, the son of Śakti [Parāśara], Vyāsa, Nārada, and Śaunaka,

1.81.s:
tṛtīyaṃ lokapālaistu caturthaṃ parikīrtitam /
lakṣaṃ japo daśāṃśena ghṛtena havanaṃ smṛtam //
1.81.d:
तृतीयं लोकपालैस्तु चतुर्थं परिकीर्तितम् ।
लक्षं जपो दशांशेन घृतेन हवनं स्मृतम् ॥
1.81.m: and the fourth is proclaimed with the guardians of the world; / one hundred thousand recitations, and fire oblation of one-tenth of that with ghee is taught.

1.81.s:
evaṃ siddhe manau mantrī prayogānapyupācaret /
śrīvṛkṣamūle deveśaṃ dhyāyanvairogiṇaṃ smaran //
1.81.d:
एवं सिद्धे मनौ मन्त्री प्रयोगानप्युपाचरेत् ।
श्रीवृक्षमूले देवेशं ध्यायन्वैरोगिणं स्मरन् ॥
1.81.m: When the mantra is thus perfected, the mantra-practitioner may perform ritual applications: / meditating on the Lord of Gods at the foot of a bilva tree, or keeping a sick person in mind,

1.81.s:
spṛṣṭvā japtvāyutaṃ sādhyaṃ smṛtvā vā manasā dvija /
rogiṇāṃ roganirmuktiṃ kuryānmantrī tu maṇḍalāt //
1.81.d:
स्पृष्ट्वा जप्त्वायुतं साध्यं स्मृत्वा वा मनसा द्विज ।
रोगिणां रोगनिर्मुक्तिं कुर्यान्मन्त्री तु मण्डलात् ॥
1.81.m: touching the subject to be cured and reciting ten thousand times, or recalling him in mind, O twice-born, / the mantra-practitioner can free the sick from illness within a period of forty days.

1.81.s:
kanyārthī juhuyāllājairbilvaiścāpi dhanāptaye /
vastrārthī gandhakusumairārogyāya tilairhunet //
1.81.d:
कन्यार्थी जुहुयाल्लाजैर्बिल्वैश्चापि धनाप्तये ।
वस्त्रार्थी गन्धकुसुमैरारोग्याय तिलैर्हुनेत् ॥
1.81.m: One seeking a maiden should offer puffed grain; and [bilva fruits] for the acquisition of wealth; / one seeking clothing should offer fragrant flowers, and sesamum seeds for health.

1.81.s:
ravivāre jale sthitvā nābhimātre japettu yaḥ /
aṣṭottarasahasraṃ vai sa jvaraṃ nāśayed dhruvam //
1.81.d:
रविवारे जले स्थित्वा नाभिमात्रे जपेत्तु यः ।
अष्टोत्तरसहस्रं वै स ज्वरं नाशयेद् ध्रुवम् ॥
1.81.m: One who stands in water up to the navel on a Sunday and recites / one thousand and eight times certainly destroys fever.

1.81.s:
vivāhārthaṃ japenmāsaṃ śaśimaṇḍalamadhyagam /
dhyātvā kṛṣṇaṃ labhetkanyāṃ vāñchitāṃ cāpi nārada //
1.81.d:
विवाहार्थं जपेन्मासं शशिमण्डलमध्यगम् ।
ध्यात्वा कृष्णं लभेत्कन्यां वाञ्छितां चापि नारद ॥
1.81.m: To obtain a marriage, one should recite for a month, meditating on Kṛṣṇa / situated in the center of the orb of the moon; then, O Nārada, he will obtain the desired maiden.

1.81.s:
vasudevapadaṃ procya nigaḍacchedaśabdataḥ /
vāsudevāya varmāstre svāhānto manurīritaḥ //
1.81.d:
वसुदेवपदं प्रोच्य निगडच्छेदशब्दतः ।
वासुदेवाय वर्मास्त्रे स्वाहान्तो मनुरीरितः ॥
1.81.m: Uttering the word 'Vasudeva', then the words 'nigaḍaccheda', / then 'Vāsudevāya', armor [huṃ], weapon [phaṭ], ending in svāhā, is the mantra declared.

1.81.s:
nārado 'sya ṛṣiśchando gāyatrī kṛṣṇadevatā /
varma bījaṃ śiraḥ śaktiranyatsarvaṃ daśārṇavat //
1.81.d:
नारदो ऽस्य ऋषिश्छन्दो गायत्री कृष्णदेवता ।
वर्म बीजं शिरः शक्तिरन्यत्सर्वं दशार्णवत् ॥
1.81.m: Its sage is Nārada, the metre is gāyatrī, the deity is Kṛṣṇa, / the armor [huṃ] is the bīja, the head [svāhā] is the śakti, and everything else is like the ten-syllabled mantra.

1.81.s:
bālaḥ pavanadīrghaiduyukto jhiṇṭīśayurjalam /
atrirvyāsāya hṛdayaṃ manuraṣṭākṣaro 'vatu //
1.81.d:
बालः पवनदीर्घैदुयुक्तो झिण्टीशयुर्जलम् ।
अत्रिर्व्यासाय हृदयं मनुरष्टाक्षरो ऽवतु ॥
1.81.m: […] 'Vyāsāya hṛdayam' [namaḥ]: may this eight-syllabled mantra protect!

1.81.s:
brāhmānuṣṭup muniśchando devaḥ satyavatīsutaḥ /
ādyaṃ bījaṃ namaḥ śaktidīrghāḍhyo nādināṅgakam //
1.81.d:
ब्राह्मानुष्टुप् मुनिश्छन्दो देवः सत्यवतीसुतः ।
आद्यं बीजं नमः शक्तिदीर्घाढ्यो नादिनाङ्गकम् ॥
1.81.m: Brahmā is the sage, the metre is anuṣṭubh, and the deity is the son of Satyavatī [Vyāsa]. / The first [syllable] is the seed, ‘namaḥ’ is the energy, and with the long vowels and the nasal sound, the limbs [are formed].

1.81.s:
vyākhyāmudrikayā lasatkaratalaṃ sadyogapīṭhasthitaṃ vāme jānutale dadhānamaparaṃ hastaṃ suvidyānidhim /
vipravrātavṛtaṃ prasannamanasaṃ pāthoruhāṅgadyutiṃ pārāśaryyamatīva puṇyacaritaṃ vyāsaṃ smaretsiddhaye //
1.81.d:
व्याख्यामुद्रिकया लसत्करतलं सद्योगपीठस्थितं वामे जानुतले दधानमपरं हस्तं सुविद्यानिधिम् ।
विप्रव्रातवृतं प्रसन्नमनसं पाथोरुहाङ्गद्युतिं पाराशर्य्यमतीव पुण्यचरितं व्यासं स्मरेत्सिद्धये ॥
1.81.m: Whose palm shines with the exposition gesture, seated on an excellent yoga-pīṭha, holding his other hand upon his left knee, a treasure-house of noble knowledge, / surrounded by a multitude of brahmins, serene in mind, with the bodily lustre of a lotus, Pārāśarya whose conduct is exceedingly virtuous—one should meditate upon Vyāsa for attainment.

1.81.s:
japedaṣṭasahasrāṇi pāyasairhemamācaret /
pūrvoktapīṭhe vyāsasya pūrvamaṅgāni pūjayet //
1.81.d:
जपेदष्टसहस्राणि पायसैर्हेममाचरेत् ।
पूर्वोक्तपीठे व्यासस्य पूर्वमङ्गानि पूजयेत् ॥
1.81.m: He should recite [the mantra] eight thousand times and perform fire oblations with milk-rice. / On the previously mentioned pīṭha, he should first worship the limbs of Vyāsa.

1.81.s:
prācyādiṣu yajetpailaṃ vaiśaṃpāyanajaiminī /
sumaṃptuṃ koṇabhāgeṣu śrīśukaṃ romaharṣaṇam //
1.81.d:
प्राच्यादिषु यजेत्पैलं वैशंपायनजैमिनी ।
सुमंप्तुं कोणभागेषु श्रीशुकं रोमहर्षणम् ॥
1.81.m: In the east and the other directions, he should worship Paila, Vaiśaṃpāyana, Jaimini, / and Sumantu; in the corner directions, the glorious Śuka, Romaharṣaṇa,

1.81.s:
ugraśravasamanyāṃśca munīnseṃdrādikāyayudhān /
evaṃ siddhamanurmantrī kavitvaṃ śobhanāḥ prajāḥ //
1.81.d:
उग्रश्रवसमन्यांश्च मुनीन्सेंद्रादिकाययुधान् ।
एवं सिद्धमनुर्मन्त्री कवित्वं शोभनाः प्रजाः ॥
1.81.m: and Ugraśravas, as well as the other sages, together with Indra and the other [guardians] and their weapons. / Thus having mastered the mantra, the practitioner of the mantra attains poetic skill, excellent progeny,

1.81.s:
vyākhyānaśaktiṃ kīrtiṃ ca labhate saṃpadāṃ cayam /
nṛsiṃho mādhavo dṛṣṭo lohito nigamādimaḥ //
1.81.d:
व्याख्यानशक्तिं कीर्तिं च लभते संपदां चयम् ।
नृसिंहो माधवो दृष्टो लोहितो निगमादिमः ॥
1.81.m: the power of exposition, renown, and an accumulation of riches. / ‘Nṛsiṃha’, ‘Mādhava’, ‘dṛṣṭa’, ‘lohita’, the first of the Vedas [oṃ],

1.81.s:
kṛśānujāyā pañcārṇo manurviṣaharaḥ paraḥ /
anantapaṅktipakṣīndrā muniśchandaḥ surā matāḥ //
1.81.d:
कृशानुजाया पञ्चार्णो मनुर्विषहरः परः ।
अनन्तपङ्क्तिपक्षीन्द्रा मुनिश्छन्दः सुरा मताः ॥
1.81.m: and the wife of fire [svāhā] is the supreme five-syllabled mantra that destroys poison. / Ananta, paṅkti, and the king of birds [Garuḍa] are considered the sage, metre, and deity.

1.81.s:
tāravahnipriye bījaśaktī mantrasya kīrtite /
jvalajvala mahāmantrī svāhā hṛdayamīritam //
1.81.d:
तारवह्निप्रिये बीजशक्ती मन्त्रस्य कीर्तिते ।
ज्वलज्वल महामन्त्री स्वाहा हृदयमीरितम् ॥
1.81.m: Tāra [oṃ] and the beloved of fire [svāhā] are stated to be the seed and the energy of the mantra. / ‘Jvala jvala mahāmantrī svāhā’ is declared to be the heart.

1.81.s:
garuḍeti padasyānte cūḍānanaśucipriyā /
śiromantro garuḍataḥ śikhe svāhā śikhā manuḥ //
1.81.d:
गरुडेति पदस्यान्ते चूडाननशुचिप्रिया ।
शिरोमन्त्रो गरुडतः शिखे स्वाहा शिखा मनुः ॥
1.81.m: After the word ‘garuḍa’, ‘cūḍānana’ and the beloved of the pure [svāhā] / is the head mantra; from ‘garuḍa’, ‘śikhe svāhā’ is the śikhā mantra.

1.81.s:
garuḍeti padaṃ procya prabhañjayayugaṃ vadet /
prabhedayayugaṃ paścādvitrāsaya vimardaya //
1.81.d:
गरुडेति पदं प्रोच्य प्रभञ्जययुगं वदेत् ।
प्रभेदययुगं पश्चाद्वित्रासय विमर्दय ॥
1.81.m: Uttering the word ‘garuḍa’, one should say the pair of ‘prabhañjaya’, / then the pair of ‘prabhedaya’, ‘vitrāsaya’, ‘vimardaya’,

1.81.s:
pratyekaṃ dvistataḥ svāhā kavacasya manurmataḥ /
ugrarūpadharānte tu sarvaviṣahareti ca //
1.81.d:
प्रत्येकं द्विस्ततः स्वाहा कवचस्य मनुर्मतः ।
उग्ररूपधरान्ते तु सर्वविषहरेति च ॥
1.81.m: each twice, and then ‘svāhā’ is considered the mantra of the armour. / After ‘ugrarūpadhara’, then ‘sarvaviṣahara’,

1.81.s:
bhīṣayadvitayaṃ procya sarvaṃ dahadaheti ca /
bhasmīkuru tataḥ svāhā netramantro 'yamīritaḥ //
1.81.d:
भीषयद्वितयं प्रोच्य सर्वं दहदहेति च ।
भस्मीकुरु ततः स्वाहा नेत्रमन्त्रो ऽयमीरितः ॥
1.81.m: and uttering the pair of ‘bhīṣaya’, then ‘sarvaṃ daha daha’ / and ‘bhasmīkuru’, followed by ‘svāhā’—this is declared to be the eye mantra.

1.81.s:
apratihatavarṇānte balāya prahateti ca /
śāsanānte tathā huṃ phaṭ svāhāstramanurīritaḥ //
1.81.d:
अप्रतिहतवर्णान्ते बलाय प्रहतेति च ।
शासनान्ते तथा हुं फट् स्वाहास्त्रमनुरीरितः ॥
1.81.m: After the syllables ‘apratihata’, ‘balāya prahata’, / and after ‘śāsana’, likewise ‘huṃ phaṭ svāhā’ is declared to be the weapon mantra.

1.81.s: pāde kaṭau hṛdi mukhe mūrdhniṃ varṇānpravinyaset //
1.81.d: पादे कटौ हृदि मुखे मूर्ध्निं वर्णान्प्रविन्यसेत् ॥
1.81.m: One should place the syllables on the feet, waist, heart, mouth, and head.

1.81.s:
taptasvarṇanibhaṃ phaṇīndranikaraiḥkḷptāṅga bhūṣaṃprabhuṃ startṛāṇāṃ śamayantamugramakhilaṃ nṝṇāṃ viṣaṃ tatkṣaṇāt /
cañcvagrapracaladbhujaṅgamabhayaṃ pāṇyorvaraṃ bibhrataṃ pakṣoccāritasāmagītamamalaṃ śrīpakṣirājaṃ bhaje //
1.81.d:
तप्तस्वर्णनिभं फणीन्द्रनिकरैःकॢप्ताङ्ग भूषंप्रभुं स्तर्तृआणां शमयन्तमुग्रमखिलं नॄणां विषं तत्क्षणात् ।
चञ्च्वग्रप्रचलद्भुजङ्गमभयं पाण्योर्वरं बिभ्रतं पक्षोच्चारितसामगीतममलं श्रीपक्षिराजं भजे ॥
1.81.m: Resembling molten gold, his bodily ornaments formed of heaps of serpent-kings, the lord who instantly dispels all fierce poison from men who praise him, / terrifying snakes that flutter at the tip of his beak, bearing a boon in his hands, whose pure wings chant the Sāmaveda songs—I revere the glorious king of birds.

1.81.s:
pañcalakṣaṃ japenmantraṃ daśāṃśaṃ juhuyāttilaiḥ /
pūjayenmātṛkāpīṭhe garuḍaṃ vedavigraham //
1.81.d:
पञ्चलक्षं जपेन्मन्त्रं दशांशं जुहुयात्तिलैः ।
पूजयेन्मातृकापीठे गरुडं वेदविग्रहम् ॥
1.81.m: He should recite the mantra five hundred thousand times, and offer a tenth part in fire oblations with sesamum seeds. / On the mātṛkā-pīṭha he should worship Garuḍa, the embodiment of the Vedas.

1.81.s:
caturthyantaḥ pakṣirājaḥ svāhā pīṭhamanuḥ smṛtaḥ /
dṛṣṭvāṅgaṃ karṇikāmadhye nāgānyantreṣu pūjayet //
1.81.d:
चतुर्थ्यन्तः पक्षिराजः स्वाहा पीठमनुः स्मृतः ।
दृष्ट्वाङ्गं कर्णिकामध्ये नागान्यन्त्रेषु पूजयेत् ॥
1.81.m: ‘Pakṣirāja’ in the dative with ‘svāhā’ is remembered as the pīṭha mantra. / Having visualized the limbs in the middle of the pericarp, he should worship the serpents in the diagrams.

1.81.s:
tadbihirlokapālāṃśca vajrādyairvilasatkarān /
evaṃ siddhamanurmantrī nāśayedgaraladvayam /
dehānte labhate cāpiśrīviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne tṛtīyapāde kṛṣṇādimantrabhedanirūpaṇaṃ nāmaikāśītitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.81.d:
तद्बिहिर्लोकपालांश्च वज्राद्यैर्विलसत्करान् ।
एवं सिद्धमनुर्मन्त्री नाशयेद्गरलद्वयम् ।
देहान्ते लभते चापिश्रीविष्णोः परमं पदम् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने तृतीयपादे कृष्णादिमन्त्रभेदनिरूपणं नामैकाशीतितमो ऽध्यायः
1.81.m:
Outside that, [he should worship] the world-guardians whose hands shine with the thunderbolt and other [weapons]. / Thus having mastered the mantra, the practitioner destroys both kinds of poison, / and at the end of the body he attains the supreme abode of the glorious Viṣṇu.

Thus ends the eighty-first chapter, named the Description of the Varieties of Mantras of Kṛṣṇa and Others, in the third quarter of the Bṛhadupākhyāna in the first part of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

1.82.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca
kiṃ tvaṃ nārada jānāsi pūrvajanmani yattvayā /
prāptaṃ bhagavataḥ sākṣācchūlino yugalātmakam //
1.82.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच
किं त्वं नारद जानासि पूर्वजन्मनि यत्त्वया ।
प्राप्तं भगवतः साक्षाच्छूलिनो युगलात्मकम् ॥
1.82.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Do you know, O Nārada, what was obtained by you in a previous birth / directly from the lord who wields the trident [Śiva], consisting of the divine pair,

1.82.s:
kṛṣṇamantrarahasyaṃ ca smara vismṛtimāgatam /
sūta uvāca
ityukto nārado viprāḥ kumāreṇa tu dhīmatā //
1.82.d:
कृष्णमन्त्ररहस्यं च स्मर विस्मृतिमागतम् ।
सूत उवाच
इत्युक्तो नारदो विप्राः कुमारेण तु धीमता ॥
1.82.m: and the secret mantra of Kṛṣṇa? Recall what has been forgotten! / Sūta said: / Thus addressed, O brahmins, by the wise Kumāra,

1.82.s:
dhyāne vivedāśu ciraṃ caritaṃ pūrvajanmanaḥ /
tataściraṃ dhyānaparo nārado bhagavatpriyaḥ //
1.82.d:
ध्याने विवेदाशु चिरं चरितं पूर्वजन्मनः ।
ततश्चिरं ध्यानपरो नारदो भगवत्प्रियः ॥
1.82.m: Nārada, in meditation, quickly came to know the long past story of his former birth. / Then, intent on meditation for a long time, Nārada, beloved of the Lord,

1.82.s:
jñātvā sarvaṃ suvṛttāntaṃ suprasannānano 'bravīt /
bhagavansarvavṛttāntaḥ pūrvakalpasamudbavaḥ //
1.82.d:
ज्ञात्वा सर्वं सुवृत्तान्तं सुप्रसन्नाननो ऽब्रवीत् ।
भगवन्सर्ववृत्तान्तः पूर्वकल्पसमुद्बवः ॥
1.82.m: knowing the entire account well, said with a delighted face: / ‘O Lord, the whole account arising from the previous aeon

1.82.s:
mama smṛtimanuprāpto vinā yugalalaṃbhanam /
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya nāradasya mahātmanaḥ //
1.82.d:
मम स्मृतिमनुप्राप्तो विना युगललंभनम् ।
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य नारदस्य महात्मनः ॥
1.82.m: has returned to my memory, except for the attainment of the divine pair.’ / Hearing those words of the great-souled Nārada,

1.82.s:
sanatkumāro bhagavān vyājahāra yathātatham /
sanatkumāra uvāca
śṛṇu vipra pravakṣyāmi yasmiñjanmani śūlinaḥ //
1.82.d:
सनत्कुमारो भगवान् व्याजहार यथातथम् ।
सनत्कुमार उवाच
शृणु विप्र प्रवक्ष्यामि यस्मिञ्जन्मनि शूलिनः ॥
1.82.m: the blessed Sanatkumāra spoke as it truly was. / Sanatkumāra said: / Listen, O brahmin, I shall tell you in which birth from the trident-wielder

1.82.s:
prāptaṃ kṛṣṇarahasyaṃ vai sāvadhāno bhavādhunā /
asmātsārasvatātkalpātpūrvasminpañcaviṃśake //
1.82.d:
प्राप्तं कृष्णरहस्यं वै सावधानो भवाधुना ।
अस्मात्सारस्वतात्कल्पात्पूर्वस्मिन्पञ्चविंशके ॥
1.82.m: the secret of Kṛṣṇa was indeed obtained. Be attentive now! / Prior to this present Sārasvata aeon, in the twenty-fifth

1.82.s:
kalpe tvaṃ kāśyapo jāto nārado nāma nāmataḥ /
tatraikadā tvaṃ kailāsaṃ prāptaḥ kṛṣṇasya yoginaḥ //
1.82.d:
कल्पे त्वं काश्यपो जातो नारदो नाम नामतः ।
तत्रैकदा त्वं कैलासं प्राप्तः कृष्णस्य योगिनः ॥
1.82.m: aeon, you were born as a Kāśyapa named Nārada by name. / There, once, you reached Kailāsa to ask of the yogin Kṛṣṇa,

1.82.s:
saṃpraṣṭuṃ paramaṃ tatvaṃ śivaṃ kailāsavāsinam /
tvayā pṛṣṭo mahādevo rahasyaṃ svaprakāśitam //
1.82.d:
संप्रष्टुं परमं तत्वं शिवं कैलासवासिनम् ।
त्वया पृष्टो महादेवो रहस्यं स्वप्रकाशितम् ॥
1.82.m: to ask Śiva, the dweller of Kailāsa, about the supreme truth. / Questioned by you, Mahādeva, in accordance with the truth,

1.82.s:
kathayāmāsa tatvena nityalīlānugaṃ hareḥ /
tatastadante tu punastvayā vijñāpito haraḥ //
1.82.d:
कथयामास तत्वेन नित्यलीलानुगं हरेः ।
ततस्तदन्ते तु पुनस्त्वया विज्ञापितो हरः ॥
1.82.m: related the secret revealed by himself, which follows the eternal pastimes of Hari. / Then, at the end of that, Hara was again petitioned by you

1.82.s:
nityāṃ līlāṃ harerdraṣṭuṃ tataḥ prāha sadāśivaḥ /
gopījanapadasyānte vallabheti padaṃ tataḥ //
1.82.d:
नित्यां लीलां हरेर्द्रष्टुं ततः प्राह सदाशिवः ।
गोपीजनपदस्यान्ते वल्लभेति पदं ततः ॥
1.82.m: in order to see the eternal pastimes of Hari; then Sadāśiva said: / ‘After the word “gopījana”, then the word “vallabha”,

1.82.s:
caraṇāccharaṇaṃ paścātprapadye iti vai manuḥ /
mantrasyāsya ṛṣiḥ prokto surabhiśchanda eva ca //
1.82.d:
चरणाच्छरणं पश्चात्प्रपद्ये इति वै मनुः ।
मन्त्रस्यास्य ऋषिः प्रोक्तो सुरभिश्छन्द एव च ॥
1.82.m: then from “caraṇāt” to “śaraṇaṃ prapadye”—this is indeed the mantra. / The sage of this mantra is declared to be Surabhi, the metre is

1.82.s:
gāyatrī devatā cāsya ballavīvallabho vibhuḥ /
prapanno 'smīti tadbhaktau viniyoga udāhṛtaḥ //
1.82.d:
गायत्री देवता चास्य बल्लवीवल्लभो विभुः ।
प्रपन्नो ऽस्मीति तद्भक्तौ विनियोग उदाहृतः ॥
1.82.m: gāyatrī, and its deity is the all-pervading Beloved of the cowherd maidens. / The application is declared with “I have taken refuge” in devotion to him.

1.82.s:
nāsya siddhādikaṃ vipra śodhanaṃ nyāsakalpanam /
kevalaṃ cintanaṃ sadyo nityalīlāprakāśakam //
1.82.d:
नास्य सिद्धादिकं विप्र शोधनं न्यासकल्पनम् ।
केवलं चिन्तनं सद्यो नित्यलीलाप्रकाशकम् ॥
1.82.m: It has no [requirement of] purification such as “siddha” and the like, O brahmin, nor any prescription of ritual placement; / mere contemplation immediately reveals the eternal pastimes.

1.82.s: ābhyantarasya dharmasya sādhanaṃ vacmi sāṃpratam //
1.82.d: आभ्यन्तरस्य धर्मस्य साधनं वच्मि सांप्रतम् ॥
1.82.m: I shall now speak of the practice of the internal duty.

1.82.s:
saṃgṛhya mantraṃ gurubhaktiyukto vicintya sarvaṃ manasā tadīhitam /
kṛpāṃ tadīyāṃ nijadharmasaṃstho vibhāvayannātmani toṣayedgurum //
1.82.d:
संगृह्य मन्त्रं गुरुभक्तियुक्तो विचिन्त्य सर्वं मनसा तदीहितम् ।
कृपां तदीयां निजधर्मसंस्थो विभावयन्नात्मनि तोषयेद्गुरुम् ॥
1.82.m: Having received the mantra, endowed with devotion to the guru, pondering all his wishes with the mind, / meditating upon his grace in oneself while steadfast in one’s own duty, one should please the guru.

1.82.s:
satāḥ śikṣeta vai dharmāṃnprapannānāṃ bhayāpahān /
aihikāmuṣmikīcintāvidhurān siddhidāyakān //
1.82.d:
सताः शिक्षेत वै धर्मांन्प्रपन्नानां भयापहान् ।
ऐहिकामुष्मिकीचिन्ताविधुरान् सिद्धिदायकान् ॥
1.82.m: One should learn the practices of the virtuous that remove the fears of the surrendered, / free from worldly and other-worldly worries, conferring spiritual attainments.

1.82.s:
sveṣṭadevadhiyā nityaṃ toṣayedvaiṣṇavāṃstathā /
bhartsanādikameteṣāṃ na kadācidvicintayet //
1.82.d:
स्वेष्टदेवधिया नित्यं तोषयेद्वैष्णवांस्तथा ।
भर्त्सनादिकमेतेषां न कदाचिद्विचिन्तयेत् ॥
1.82.m: With the mindset that they are one's chosen deity, one should always please the Vaiṣṇavas; / one should never think of censuring them and the like.

1.82.s:
pūrvakarmavaśādbhavyamaihikaṃ bhogyameva ca /
āyuṣyakaṃ tathā kṛṣṇaḥ svayameva kariṣyati //
1.82.d:
पूर्वकर्मवशाद्भव्यमैहिकं भोग्यमेव च ।
आयुष्यकं तथा कृष्णः स्वयमेव करिष्यति ॥
1.82.m: Whatever is to be experienced in this world will occur by the power of past deeds; / likewise, Kṛṣṇa himself will take care of one’s lifespan.

1.82.s:
śrīkṛṣṇaṃ nityalīlāsthaṃ cintayetsvadhiyāniśam /
śrīmadarcāvatāreṇa kṛṣṇaṃ paricaretsadā //
1.82.d:
श्रीकृष्णं नित्यलीलास्थं चिन्तयेत्स्वधियानिशम् ।
श्रीमदर्चावतारेण कृष्णं परिचरेत्सदा ॥
1.82.m: Day and night one should meditate with one’s intellect on the glorious Kṛṣṇa abiding in eternal pastimes; / one should always serve Kṛṣṇa in the glorious form of the icon-incarnation.

1.82.s:
ananyacintanīyo 'sau prapannaiḥ śaraṇārthibhiḥ /
stheyaṃ ca dehagehādāvudāsīnatayā budhaiḥ //
1.82.d:
अनन्यचिन्तनीयो ऽसौ प्रपन्नैः शरणार्थिभिः ।
स्थेयं च देहगेहादावुदासीनतया बुधैः ॥
1.82.m: He alone should be contemplated with undivided focus by those who have taken refuge, seeking shelter; / and the wise should remain detached from the body, home, and the like.

1.82.s:
guroravajñāṃ sādhūnāṃ nindāṃ bhedaṃ hare harau /
vedanindāṃ harernāmabalātpāpasamīhanam //
1.82.d:
गुरोरवज्ञां साधूनां निन्दां भेदं हरे हरौ ।
वेदनिन्दां हरेर्नामबलात्पापसमीहनम् ॥
1.82.m: Disrespect toward the guru, slander of the virtuous, seeing difference between Hari and Hara, / slander of the Vedas, undertaking sin on the strength of the name of Hari,

1.82.s:
arthavādaṃ harer nāmni pāṣaṇḍaṃ nāmasaṃgrahe /
alase nāstike caiva harināmopadeśanam //
1.82.d:
अर्थवादं हरेर् नाम्नि पाषण्डं नामसंग्रहे ।
अलसे नास्तिके चैव हरिनामोपदेशनम् ॥
1.82.m: treating Hari’s name as mere praise, heresy in the recitation of the name, / teaching Hari’s name to the lazy and the atheist,

1.82.s:
nāmavismaraṇaṃ cāpi nāmnyanādarameva ca /
saṃtyajed dūrato vatsa doṣānetānsudāruṇān //
1.82.d:
नामविस्मरणं चापि नाम्न्यनादरमेव च ।
संत्यजेद् दूरतो वत्स दोषानेतान्सुदारुणान् ॥
1.82.m: forgetting the name, and disrespect toward the name— / one should avoid these terrible faults from afar, O child!

1.82.s:
prapanno 'smīti satataṃ cintayeddhṛdgataṃ harim /
sa eva pālanaṃ nityaṃ kariṣyati mameti ca //
1.82.d:
प्रपन्नो ऽस्मीति सततं चिन्तयेद्धृद्गतं हरिम् ।
स एव पालनं नित्यं करिष्यति ममेति च ॥
1.82.m: Constantly thinking “I have surrendered”, one should contemplate Hari dwelling in the heart, / and [reflect]: “He alone will always protect me.”

1.82.s:
tavāsmi rādhikānātha karmaṇā manasā girā /
kṛṣṇakānteti caivāsmi yuvāmeva gatirmama //
1.82.d:
तवास्मि राधिकानाथ कर्मणा मनसा गिरा ।
कृष्णकान्तेति चैवास्मि युवामेव गतिर्मम ॥
1.82.m: “I am yours, O Lord of Rādhikā, in deed, thought, and word; / and I am yours, O beloved of Kṛṣṇa! You two alone are my refuge.”

1.82.s:
dāsāḥ sakhāyaḥ pitaraḥ preyasyaśca hareriha /
sarve nityā muniśreṣṭha cintanīyā mahātmabhiḥ //
1.82.d:
दासाः सखायः पितरः प्रेयस्यश्च हरेरिह ।
सर्वे नित्या मुनिश्रेष्ठ चिन्तनीया महात्मभिः ॥
1.82.m: The servants, friends, parents, and beloved women of Hari here [on earth]— / all are eternal, O best of sages, and should be contemplated by great souls.

1.82.s:
gamanāgamane nityakaroti vanagoṣṭayoḥ /
gocāraṇaṃ vayasyaiśca vināsuravighātanam //
1.82.d:
गमनागमने नित्यकरोति वनगोष्टयोः ।
गोचारणं वयस्यैश्च विनासुरविघातनम् ॥
1.82.m: He constantly goes and comes between the forest and the cow-pens; / he herds the cows with his companions, except when slaying demons.

1.82.s:
sakhāyo dvādaśākhyātā hareḥ śrīdāmapūrvakāḥ /
rādhikāyāḥ suśīlādyāḥ sakhyo dvātriṃśadīritāḥ //
1.82.d:
सखायो द्वादशाख्याता हरेः श्रीदामपूर्वकाः ।
राधिकायाः सुशीलाद्याः सख्यो द्वात्रिंशदीरिताः ॥
1.82.m: Twelve friends of Hari are recounted, headed by Śrīdāman; / thirty-two female companions of Rādhikā are proclaimed, headed by Suśīlā.

1.82.s:
ātmānaṃ cintayedvatsa tāsāṃ madhye manoramām /
rūpayauvanasaṃpannāṃ kiśorīṃ ca svalaṅkṛtām //
1.82.d:
आत्मानं चिन्तयेद्वत्स तासां मध्ये मनोरमाम् ।
रूपयौवनसंपन्नां किशोरीं च स्वलङ्कृताम् ॥
1.82.m: Among them, my child, one should imagine oneself as a delightful / young maiden endowed with beauty and youth, well adorned,

1.82.s:
nānāśilpakalābhijñāṃ kṛṣṇabhogānurūpiṇīm /
tatsevanasukhāhlādabhāvenātisunirvṛtām //
1.82.d:
नानाशिल्पकलाभिज्ञां कृष्णभोगानुरूपिणीम् ।
तत्सेवनसुखाह्लादभावेनातिसुनिर्वृताम् ॥
1.82.m: skilled in various crafts and arts, suited for Kṛṣṇa's pleasure, / completely blissful in the disposition of delight in serving him.

1.82.s:
brāhmaṃ muhūrtamārabhya yāvadardhaniśā bhavet /
tāvatparicarettau tu yathākālānusevayā //
1.82.d:
ब्राह्मं मुहूर्तमारभ्य यावदर्धनिशा भवेत् ।
तावत्परिचरेत्तौ तु यथाकालानुसेवया ॥
1.82.m: Beginning from the hour of Brahmā until midnight comes, / one should attend upon the two of them with service suited to each time.

1.82.s:
sahasraṃ ca tayornnāmnāṃ paṭhennityaṃ samāhitaḥ /
etasādhanamuddiṣṭaṃ prapannānāṃ munīśvara //
1.82.d:
सहस्रं च तयोर्न्नाम्नां पठेन्नित्यं समाहितः ।
एतसाधनमुद्दिष्टं प्रपन्नानां मुनीश्वर ॥
1.82.m: With a concentrated mind, one should daily recite the thousand names of both; / this spiritual practice is taught for those who have taken refuge, O lord of sages.

1.82.s:
nākhyeyaṃ kasyacittubhyaṃ mayā tattvaṃ prakāśitam /
sanatkumāra uvāca
tatastvaṃ nārada punaḥ pṛṣṭavānvai sadāśivam //
1.82.d:
नाख्येयं कस्यचित्तुभ्यं मया तत्त्वं प्रकाशितम् ।
सनत्कुमार उवाच
ततस्त्वं नारद पुनः पृष्टवान्वै सदाशिवम् ॥
1.82.m:
This must not be told to anyone; the ultimate truth has been revealed to you by me.
Sanatkumāra said:
Then, Nārada, you indeed questioned Sadāśiva again

1.82.s:
nāmnāṃ sahasraṃ taccāpi proktavāṃ stacchṛṇuṣva me /
dhyātvā vṛndāvane ramye yamunātīrasaṃgatam //
1.82.d:
नाम्नां सहस्रं तच्चापि प्रोक्तवां स्तच्छृणुष्व मे ।
ध्यात्वा वृन्दावने रम्ये यमुनातीरसंगतम् ॥
1.82.m: about that thousand of names, and he too spoke it; hear that from me. / Having meditated on [him] assembled on the bank of the Yamunā in beautiful Vṛndāvana,

1.82.s:
kalpavṛkṣaṃ samāśritya tiṣṭhantaṃ rādhikāyutam /
paṭhennāmasahasraṃ tu yugalākhyaṃ mahāmune //
1.82.d:
कल्पवृक्षं समाश्रित्य तिष्ठन्तं राधिकायुतम् ।
पठेन्नामसहस्रं तु युगलाख्यं महामुने ॥
1.82.m: standing by a wish-granting tree accompanied by Rādhikā, / one should recite the thousand names named 'The Pair', O great sage:

1.82.s:
devakīnandanaḥ śaurirvāsudevo balānujaḥ /
gadāgrajaḥ kaṃsamohaḥ kaṃsasevakamohanaḥ //
1.82.d:
देवकीनन्दनः शौरिर्वासुदेवो बलानुजः ।
गदाग्रजः कंसमोहः कंससेवकमोहनः ॥
1.82.m: Delight of Devakī, Śauri, Vāsudeva, Younger Brother of Bala, / Elder Brother of Gada, Delusion of Kaṃsa, Deluder of Kaṃsa's Servants,

1.82.s:
bhinnargalaḥ bhinnalohaḥ pitṛbāhyaḥ pitṛstutaḥ /
mātṛstutaḥ śivadhyeyo yamunājalabhedanaḥ //
1.82.d:
भिन्नर्गलः भिन्नलोहः पितृबाह्यः पितृस्तुतः ।
मातृस्तुतः शिवध्येयो यमुनाजलभेदनः ॥
1.82.m: He whose bolts were shattered, He whose irons were broken, Carried by his Father, Praised by his Father, / Praised by his Mother, Meditated upon by Śiva, Cleaver of the Waters of the Yamunā,

1.82.s:
vrajavāsī vrajānandī nandabālo dayānidhiḥ /
līlābālaḥ padmanetro gokulotsava īśvaraḥ //
1.82.d:
व्रजवासी व्रजानन्दी नन्दबालो दयानिधिः ।
लीलाबालः पद्मनेत्रो गोकुलोत्सव ईश्वरः ॥
1.82.m: Dweller in Vraja, Joy of Vraja, Boy of Nanda, Treasure of Compassion, / Playful Boy, Lotus-Eyed, Festival of Gokula, Sovereign Lord,

1.82.s:
gopikānandanaḥ kṛṣṇo gopānandaḥ satāṃ gatiḥ /
bakaprāṇaharo viṣṇurbakamuktiprado hariḥ //
1.82.d:
गोपिकानन्दनः कृष्णो गोपानन्दः सतां गतिः ।
बकप्राणहरो विष्णुर्बकमुक्तिप्रदो हरिः ॥
1.82.m: Delight of the Cowherd Women, Kṛṣṇa, Joy of Cowherds, Refuge of the Virtuous, / Taker of Baka's Life, Viṣṇu, Giver of Liberation to Baka, Hari,

1.82.s:
baladolāśayaśayaḥ śyāmalaḥ sarvasuṃdaraḥ /
padmanābho hṛṣīkeśaḥ krīḍāmanujabālakaḥ //
1.82.d:
बलदोलाशयशयः श्यामलः सर्वसुंदरः ।
पद्मनाभो हृषीकेशः क्रीडामनुजबालकः ॥
1.82.m: Resting in the Cradle of Bala, Dark-Hued, All-Beautiful, / Lotus-Navelled, Hṛṣīkeśa, Human Child in Play,

1.82.s:
līlāvidhvastaśakaṭo vedamantrābhiṣecitaḥ /
yaśodānandanaḥ kānto munikoṭiniṣevitaḥ //
1.82.d:
लीलाविध्वस्तशकटो वेदमन्त्राभिषेचितः ।
यशोदानन्दनः कान्तो मुनिकोटिनिषेवितः ॥
1.82.m: Shatterer of the Cart in Play, Consecrated with Vedic Mantras, / Delight of Yaśodā, Beloved, Served by Millions of Sages,

1.82.s:
nityaṃ madhuvanāvāsī vaikuṇṭhaḥ saṃbhavaḥ kratuḥ /
ramāpatiryadupatirmurārirmadhusūdanaḥ //
1.82.d:
नित्यं मधुवनावासी वैकुण्ठः संभवः क्रतुः ।
रमापतिर्यदुपतिर्मुरारिर्मधुसूदनः ॥
1.82.m: Perpetual Dweller in Madhuvana, Vaikuṇṭha, Source of Existence, Sacrifice, / Lord of Ramā, Lord of the Yadus, Enemy of Mura, Slayer of Madhu,

1.82.s:
mādhavo mānahārī ca śrīpatirbhūdharaḥ prabhuḥ /
bṛhadvanamahālīlo nandasūnurmahāsanaḥ //
1.82.d:
माधवो मानहारी च श्रीपतिर्भूधरः प्रभुः ।
बृहद्वनमहालीलो नन्दसूनुर्महासनः ॥
1.82.m: Mādhava, Remover of Pride, Lord of Śrī, Supporter of the Earth, Master, / Great in Play in Bṛhadvana, Son of Nanda, Possessor of a Great Seat,

1.82.s:
tṛṇāvartaprāṇahārī yaśodāvismayapradaḥ /
trailokyavaktraḥ padmākṣaḥ padmahastaḥ priyaṅkaraḥ //
1.82.d:
तृणावर्तप्राणहारी यशोदाविस्मयप्रदः ।
त्रैलोक्यवक्त्रः पद्माक्षः पद्महस्तः प्रियङ्करः ॥
1.82.m: Taker of Tṛṇāvarta's Life, Giver of Wonder to Yaśodā, / Having the Three Worlds in his Mouth, Lotus-Eyed, Lotus-Handed, Beneficent,

1.82.s:
brahmaṇyo dharmagoptā ca bhūpatiḥ śrīdharaḥ svarāṭ /
ajādhyakṣaḥ śivādhyakṣo dharmādhyakṣo maheśvaraḥ //
1.82.d:
ब्रह्मण्यो धर्मगोप्ता च भूपतिः श्रीधरः स्वराट् ।
अजाध्यक्षः शिवाध्यक्षो धर्माध्यक्षो महेश्वरः ॥
1.82.m: Friendly to Brāhmaṇas, Protector of Dharma, King of the Earth, Bearer of Śrī, Self-Ruling, / Overseer of Aja, Overseer of Śiva, Overseer of Dharma, Great Lord,

1.82.s:
vedāntavedyo brahmasthaḥ prajāpatiramoghadṛk /
gopīkarāvalaṃbī ca gopabālakasupriyaḥ //
1.82.d:
वेदान्तवेद्यो ब्रह्मस्थः प्रजापतिरमोघदृक् ।
गोपीकरावलंबी च गोपबालकसुप्रियः ॥
1.82.m: Known through the Upaniṣads, Abiding in Brahman, Lord of Creatures, Infallible of Sight, / Holding the Hands of Cowherd Women, Dear Friend of Cowherd Boys,

1.82.s:
bālānuyīyī balavān śrīdāmapriya ātmavān /
gopīgṛhāṅgaṇaratirbhadraḥ suślokamaṅgalaḥ //
1.82.d:
बालानुयीयी बलवान् श्रीदामप्रिय आत्मवान् ।
गोपीगृहाङ्गणरतिर्भद्रः सुश्लोकमङ्गलः ॥
1.82.m: Following the Boys, Mighty, Dear to Śrīdāman, Self-Possessed, / Delighting in the Courtyards of Cowherd Women's Houses, Auspicious, Praised in Beautiful Verses,

1.82.s:
navanītaharo bālo navanītapriyāśanaḥ /
bālavṛndī markavṛndī cakitākṣaḥ palāyitaḥ //
1.82.d:
नवनीतहरो बालो नवनीतप्रियाशनः ।
बालवृन्दी मर्कवृन्दी चकिताक्षः पलायितः ॥
1.82.m: Stealer of Fresh Butter, Child, Fond of Eating Fresh Butter, / Surrounded by Children, Surrounded by Monkeys, Startled-Eyed, Fleeing,

1.82.s:
yaśodātarjitaḥ kaṃpī māyāruditaśobhanaḥ /
dāmodaro 'prameyātmā dayālurbhaktavatsalaḥ //
1.82.d:
यशोदातर्जितः कंपी मायारुदितशोभनः ।
दामोदरो ऽप्रमेयात्मा दयालुर्भक्तवत्सलः ॥
1.82.m: Threatened by Yaśodā, Trembling, Charming in Feigned Crying, / Dāmodara, Immeasurable-Souled, Compassionate, Loving to Devotees,

1.82.s:
subaddholūkhale namraśirā gopīkadarthitaḥ /
vṛkṣabhaṅgī śokabhaṅgī dhanadātmajamokṣaṇaḥ //
1.82.d:
सुबद्धोलूखले नम्रशिरा गोपीकदर्थितः ।
वृक्षभङ्गी शोकभङ्गी धनदात्मजमोक्षणः ॥
1.82.m: Firmly Bound to the Mortar, Bowed-Headed, Scolded by the Cowherd Woman, / Breaker of the Trees, Dispeller of Grief, Liberator of the Sons of Kuvera,

1.82.s:
devarṣivacanaślāghī bhaktavātsalyasāgaraḥ /
vrajakolāhalakaro vrajānadavivarddhanaḥ //
1.82.d:
देवर्षिवचनश्लाघी भक्तवात्सल्यसागरः ।
व्रजकोलाहलकरो व्रजानदविवर्द्धनः ॥
1.82.m: Praiser of the Words of the Divine Sage, Ocean of Affection for Devotees, / Maker of Clamour in Vraja, Increaser of Vraja's Joy,

1.82.s:
gopātmā prerakaḥ sākṣī vṛndāvananivāsakṛt /
vatsapālo vatsapatirgopadārakamaṇḍanaḥ //
1.82.d:
गोपात्मा प्रेरकः साक्षी वृन्दावननिवासकृत् ।
वत्सपालो वत्सपतिर्गोपदारकमण्डनः ॥
1.82.m: Soul of Cowherds, Instigator, Witness, Dweller in Vṛndāvana, / Protector of Calves, Lord of Calves, Ornament of Cowherd Children,

1.82.s:
bālakrīḍo bālaratirbālakaḥ kanakāṅgadī /
pītāmbaro hemamālī maṇimuktāvibhūṣaṇaḥ //
1.82.d:
बालक्रीडो बालरतिर्बालकः कनकाङ्गदी ।
पीताम्बरो हेममाली मणिमुक्ताविभूषणः ॥
1.82.m: Boyish in Play, Delighting with Boys, Child, Wearing Golden Armlets, / Clothed in Yellow Garments, Wearing a Golden Garland, Adorned with Gems and Pearls,

1.82.s:
kiṅkiṇīkaṭakī sūtrī nūpurī mudri kānvitaḥ /
vatsāsurapatidhvaṃsī bakāsuravināśanaḥ //
1.82.d:
किङ्किणीकटकी सूत्री नूपुरी मुद्रि कान्वितः ।
वत्सासुरपतिध्वंसी बकासुरविनाशनः ॥
1.82.m: Wearing Small Bells and Bracelets, Wearing a Girdle-Cord, Wearing Anklets, Wearing Rings, / Destroyer of the Lord of Vatsāsura, Destroyer of Bakāsura,

1.82.s:
aghāsuravināśī ca vinidrīkṛtabālakaḥ /
ādya ātmapradaḥ saṃgī yamunātīrabhojanaḥ //
1.82.d:
अघासुरविनाशी च विनिद्रीकृतबालकः ।
आद्य आत्मप्रदः संगी यमुनातीरभोजनः ॥
1.82.m: Destroyer of Aghāsura, He who Awakened the Boys, / Primordial, Giver of Himself, Companion, Feasting on the Bank of the Yamunā,

1.82.s:
